Validate or commit one ordered batch over color, text, effect or guide styles. Supports definition edits, apply and detach, subject to native target/override rules.

| Field | JSON type | JSON-required | Default / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

### get_request_status

`POST /v2/get_request_status`

Recover the same requestId in the original target scope: documentHandle, tabId, or neither for a session operation. Do not provide contradictory scopes. Retention is bounded; unknown does not prove that the original operation failed.

| Field | JSON type | JSON-required | Default / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `requestId` | string | yes | — |
| `documentHandle` | string / null | no | — |
| `tabId` | string / null | no | — |

Data: **{status: "pending" | "completed" | "unknown", result?: originalEnvelope}**. [Full request JSON Schema](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-schemas/get_request_status.schema.json).

### get_automation_documentation

`POST /v2/get_automation_documentation`

Read focused runtime help. topic defaults to overview; overview aliases common. Topics: common, components, styles, variables, documents, libraries. Available without an open document.

| Field | JSON type | JSON-required | Default / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `topic` | string | no | `"overview"` |

Data: **{topic, content}**. [Full request JSON Schema](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-schemas/get_automation_documentation.schema.json).

### activate_page

`POST /v2/activate_page`

Navigate explicitly to a page in the target document. It requires the current revision and request ID but does not add a content revision or undo item.

| Field | JSON type | JSON-required | Default / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pageId` | string | yes | — |
| `expectedRevision` | string | yes | — |
| `requestId` | string | yes | — |
| `documentHandle` | string | yes | — |

Data: **DocumentResult**. [Full request JSON Schema](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-schemas/activate_page.schema.json).

### manage_pages

`POST /v2/manage_pages`

Validate or commit 1–100 ordered page changes. Components-page roles and the last-page invariant are enforced before commit. One changed batch has one undo item.

| Field | JSON type | JSON-required | Default / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `validateOnly` | boolean | no | `false` |
| `changes` | array of typed union | yes | — |

| `documentHandle` | string | yes | — |

### create_document

`POST /v2/create_document`

Create and await a ready document. Without cloudDestination the result is local. Cloud creation needs an explicitly authorized destination and normal account permissions. Optional name follows the native document naming rules.

| Field | JSON type | JSON-required | Default / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string / null | no | — |
| `cloudDestination` | object / null | no | — |
| `requestId` | string | yes | — |

Data: **DocumentResult**. [Full request JSON Schema](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-schemas/create_document.schema.json).

### open_document

`POST /v2/open_document`

Provide exactly one locator: localPath or cloud. The cloud locator has documentId and optional versionId. Await native loading; reuse a matching visible document/version/path. A local path needs native filesystem access; opening a version can produce a read-only target.

| Field | JSON type | JSON-required | Default / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `localPath` | string / null | no | — |
| `cloud` | object / null | no | — |
| `requestId` | string | yes | — |

Data: **DocumentResult**. [Full request JSON Schema](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-schemas/open_document.schema.json).

### rename_document

`POST /v2/rename_document`

Rename through the document manager, retaining document identity. name must be a valid nonempty native document name. Inspect the returned name/path/save metadata.

| Field | JSON type | JSON-required | Default / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | — |
| `expectedRevision` | string | yes | — |
| `requestId` | string | yes | — |
| `documentHandle` | string | yes | — |

Data: **DocumentResult**. [Full request JSON Schema](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-schemas/rename_document.schema.json).

### reorder_tabs

`POST /v2/reorder_tabs`

Supply the exact complete set of currently visible tabIds in the desired order, without duplicates. Does not change document content.

| Field | JSON type | JSON-required | Default / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tabIds` | array of string | yes | — |
| `requestId` | string | yes | — |

Data: **DocumentResult with tabIds**. [Full request JSON Schema](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-schemas/reorder_tabs.schema.json).

### save_document

`POST /v2/save_document`

Await a native local save or actual cloud-send result. Untitled/imported/template files need destination unless allowDialog:true explicitly permits a dialog. overwrite defaults to false. Read destination, savedRevision and synchronization state; a sent/queued change is not a separate durable-storage guarantee.

| Field | JSON type | JSON-required | Default / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `destination` | string / null | no | — |
| `overwrite` | boolean | no | `false` |
| `allowDialog` | boolean | no | `false` |
| `expectedRevision` | string | yes | — |
| `requestId` | string | yes | — |
| `documentHandle` | string | yes | — |

Data: **DocumentResult**. [Full request JSON Schema](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-schemas/save_document.schema.json).

### close_document

`POST /v2/close_document`

tabId is always required. Every loaded-tab close requires its current documentHandle and expectedRevision. ifUnsaved defaults to fail; save or discard is explicit. Unloaded/failed tabs support metadata-only close with fail. A failed/cancelled save keeps the tab/recovery work. Use the same request ID to recover a lost close response.

| Field | JSON type | JSON-required | Default / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `documentHandle` | string / null | no | — |
| `expectedRevision` | string / null | no | — |
| `tabId` | string | yes | — |
| `ifUnsaved` | string | no | `"fail"` |
| `destination` | string / null | no | — |
| `overwrite` | boolean | no | `false` |
| `allowDialog` | boolean | no | `false` |
| `requestId` | string | yes | — |

Data: **DocumentResult with closed**. [Full request JSON Schema](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-schemas/close_document.schema.json).

### list_libraries

`POST /v2/list_libraries`

scope defaults to connected; available lists authorized account metadata without downloading every source. Editable cloud targets support persistent connections. A local target’s connected list is empty but it can inspect/import available assets. Metadata version may be null; obtain a loaded semantic sourceVersion through asset discovery before import.

| Field | JSON type | JSON-required | Default / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scope` | string | no | `"connected"` |
| `limit` | integer | no | `50` |
| `cursor` | string / null | no | — |
| `documentHandle` | string | yes | — |

Data: **{items: `LibraryInfo[]`, nextCursor?}**. [Full request JSON Schema](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-schemas/list_libraries.schema.json).

### connect_library

`POST /v2/connect_library`

Connect a discovered cloud source to an editable cloud target. The locator kind is cloud; id/endpoint must identify a pair discovered through existing authorized connections. Arbitrary endpoint URLs, local locators and self-connection are rejected. A local target cannot create persistent connections.

| Field | JSON type | JSON-required | Default / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `library` | object | no | — |
| `expectedRevision` | string | yes | — |
| `requestId` | string | yes | — |
| `documentHandle` | string | yes | — |

Data: **{library?: LibraryInfo, changed}**. [Full request JSON Schema](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-schemas/connect_library.schema.json).

### disconnect_library

`POST /v2/disconnect_library`

Await native disassociation from the editable cloud target. libraryId is an observed source ID. Existing imported definitions/consumers remain; this is not delete or deep detach.

| Field | JSON type | JSON-required | Default / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `libraryId` | string | no | — |
| `expectedRevision` | string | yes | — |
| `requestId` | string | yes | — |
| `documentHandle` | string | yes | — |

Data: **{library?: LibraryInfo, changed}**. [Full request JSON Schema](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-schemas/disconnect_library.schema.json).

### import_library_assets

`POST /v2/import_library_assets`

Import 1–100 explicit discovered asset references using libraryId and its observed semantic sourceVersion. Dependencies are prepared and the target changes in one undo operation. validateOnly defaults to false. Existing imported IDs are reused; a new asset does not implicitly refresh already imported dependencies.

| Field | JSON type | JSON-required | Default / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `libraryId` | string | no | — |
| `sourceVersion` | string | no | — |
| `assets` | array of object | no | — |
| `validateOnly` | boolean | no | `false` |
| `expectedRevision` | string | yes | — |
| `requestId` | string | yes | — |
| `documentHandle` | string | yes | — |

Data: **{assets: `AssetMapping[]`, changes: BatchResult, sourceVersion}**. [Full request JSON Schema](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-schemas/import_library_assets.schema.json).

### refresh_libraries

`POST /v2/refresh_libraries`

Refresh 1–100 unique explicit libraryId/version pairs. Each completed library is atomic; earlier successful libraries remain committed if a later one fails. Preserve IDs and supported overrides. Read per-item errors/results before retrying. Missing source assets are not automatically deleted.

| Field | JSON type | JSON-required | Default / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `libraries` | array of object | no | — |
| `expectedRevision` | string | yes | — |
| `requestId` | string | yes | — |
| `documentHandle` | string | yes | — |

Data: **{items: `LibraryRefreshItem[]`}**. [Full request JSON Schema](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-schemas/refresh_libraries.schema.json).

## Batch action fields

Put the following objects in their endpoint’s `changes` array. `action` is the required string discriminator. Each variant rejects undeclared properties. References, appearances and binding/property values are described in the nested types and semantic rules below.

### Component action: createFromLayers

| Field | JSON type | JSON-required | Default / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | `"createFromLayers"` | yes | — |
| `clientId` | string / null | no | — |
| `layerIds` | array of string | yes | — |
| `name` | string / null | no | — |
| `placement` | object / null | no | — |

### Component action: updateDefinition

| Field | JSON type | JSON-required | Default / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | `"updateDefinition"` | yes | — |
| `component` | resource selector (exactly one variant) | yes | — |
| `patch` | JSON value | yes | — |

## Native semantics and constraints

### Discovery and references

An asset reference has `kind`, `id`, `scope`, and applicable library/source/collection IDs. Kinds are `component`, `style`, `collection`, `theme`, and `variable`. Scopes are `local`, `imported`, `connectedLibrary`, and `availableLibrary`. Return complete references unchanged rather than reconstructing origins from names. A component's `componentId` and source `layerId` are distinct identities. Use discovery after creation when an operation needs a different identity kind.

Search and usage results are paginated; `limit` defaults to 50 and is bounded to 1–200. Cursors are opaque, tied to their query/target/revision and applicable source snapshot. A changed target/source can invalidate them. Restart the query after a cursor conflict. Do not treat an available-library metadata continuation as a global point-in-time snapshot: the native endpoint has no ETag/global snapshot, and equal update timestamps across a page boundary can omit metadata entries. This does not weaken source validation for an explicitly opened library.

`get_design_system_assets` returns a definition or an item-specific error for each input reference. Component content is deliberately bounded by `componentDepth` and work budgets. Missing, dead or inaccessible references are not live assets merely because a name or in-memory object remains.

### Components and instances

`createFromLayers` converts explicit existing source layers, preserving existing child IDs. Placement names an explicit page/parent when relocation is needed. `createInstances` requires explicit placements; no active selection is inferred. A `clientId` on an instance placement maps that creation into the batch's `clientIds` result.

`updateDefinition.patch` updates the existing source and explicitly identified direct children. Supported fields are:

```text
name size width height pos transform opacity blendMode hidden locked
lockAspect clipContent breakMask mask smoothCorners cornerRadius thickness
linePos lineCap lineJoin dash fill fills border borders shadows innerShadows
blur tint fillsId bordersId effectsId gridsId textStyleId
text fontSize kerning paragraphSpacing align valign lineHeight underline
strikethrough rtl casing binds layers
```

Each `layers` patch entry identifies an existing direct child by `id`; it cannot replace, add, remove or reorder siblings. IDs, layer types, component identities, state/property metadata, versions and library ownership cannot be overwritten. Patches cannot introduce new external image/font resources. Appearance leaves use the existing FREE representations.

Component property definitions are discriminated by `type`: `bool`, `text`, `swap`, `slot`, or `state`. Values are discriminated by `kind`: `bool`, `text`, `component`, or `state`. Swap/slot defaults are component selectors; state defaults identify one state. An explicit literal default can replace a variable-backed default even when the fallback literal is unchanged; a rename preserves that binding.

A property definition does not guess a source-node binding from its name. A later definition patch may use `binds` entries with numeric `field` and an actual property/value reference:

| Numeric field | Supported binding |
| --- | --- |
| `1` | Visibility: an owned bool property `ref`, a literal `bool`, or live bool variable `boolId`. |
| `58` | Text: an owned text property `ref`, literal `text`, or live text variable `textId`; target must be text. |
| `100` | Component source: an owned swap/slot property `ref`; target must be a source instance. |

Here `ref`, `boolId`, and `textId` contain actual IDs. A raw FREE appearance fragment does not turn arbitrary strings into typed batch `clientRef` selectors. Use `apply_variable_changes` for other native variable binding locations. State properties select through `setInstanceProperties` rather than a guessed source-node bind.

`combineStates` requires compatible sibling components and migrates property definitions to the shared owner. `createState` turns a standalone definition into a state group when needed. State names can encode multiple dimensions joined with `+`. `deleteState` preserves at least one state; its default policy is `rejectIfUsed`, while `replaceInstances` requires an explicit sibling replacement. Deleting a component defaults to `rejectIfUsed`; `detachInstances` is explicit.

`removeOverrides.properties` accepts the native categories below. Omit the list to remove supported overrides as a whole; `"all"` is not a category. Size reset also resets instance scale.

```text
size nestedComponent instanceSettings themes prototypingComponent text
layoutGuideStyle image flows tint color textColor textWeight cornerRadius
fills borders thickness linePos dash lineCap lineJoin effects blending
inlines exportOptions lock visibility clipContent smoothCorners startArrowhead
endArrowhead layoutOrientation layoutSpacing layoutPadding layoutAlign layoutSizing
layoutTextBaseline layoutIncludeBorders layoutReverseZIndex layoutStretch arc
layoutWrap layoutWrapDistribute layoutWrapSpacing lockAspect starRatio vertexCount
layoutMinMax imageFilters textBehavior layoutGuides textTruncate textMaxLines
scrollBehavior keepScroll name fillStyle borderStyle effectStyle textStyle
textVerticalTrim scrollOverflow binds
```

`detachInstances` materializes one level as frames while retaining nested instances. `deepDetachInstances` materializes the nested instance tree.

Source graph preparation observes the ordered batch. Every prefix that eagerly rebuilds instances must be acyclic, even if a later action would break the cycle. Order materialization and deletion around retained dependencies, or split the work and inspect resulting consumers first. Deleting a source retained by shallow materialization can return `ResourceInUse`; it never silently skips consumers. Swap compatibility follows native source name/type/sibling policy rather than position alone.

Imported definitions are read-only; local instances of imported definitions can use supported operations. Locked/generated targets and operations requiring unsupported comment relocation are rejected. Text/font/layout work must finish before publication; active text editing or an overlapping refresh can return `Busy`. These methods do not select layers, switch drawing tools, zoom, or open rename panels.

### Styles

Types are `color`, `text`, `effect`, and `guide`. `value` and `patch` use the FREE appearance fields appropriate to that kind, such as `{"fill":"0A84FF"}` for a color style. Updates keep IDs, untouched properties, variable references and linked consumers. Use `rename` rather than an appearance patch to change a name. `createFromLayer.slot` can be omitted for the native slot implied by the style type.

| Style kind | Target slot | Eligible target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | `fills` or `borders` | Native style-bearing layer; supported text fills can include a range. |
| `text` | `text` | Text layer. |
| `effect` | `effects` | Eligible native layer. |
| `guide` | `guides` | Frame. |

A target has explicit `layerId`; its parser default slot is `fills`, so provide the appropriate slot for other kinds. Ranges use `start`/`length` in UTF-16 positions and must not split a character. Other slots do not accept ranges.

`delete` defaults to `rejectIfUsed`; `detachConsumers` materializes supported effective appearance. `detach` materializes the explicit targets. Whole generated text style operations can use native overrides; partial generated ranges require a matching existing full inline override. A detach that would freeze unrelated inherited fields can be unsupported. Numeric scaled effects can be materialized where native geometry can preserve them, while incompatible scaled variable-bound effects are rejected. Imported style definitions cannot be edited directly.

### Variables, aliases and bindings

Types are `color`, `float`, `bool`, and `text`. Literal values are respectively FREE color strings, finite JSON numbers, JSON booleans, and strings. For example:

```json
{"kind":"literal","value":"0A84FF"}
```

```json
{"kind":"alias","variable":{"id":"<same-type-variable-id>"}}
```

Aliases are typed references, not strings containing IDs. Values belong to explicit themes in the variable's collection. `createTheme` clones a required source theme. Native collection/theme/default-role rules, alias type rules and graph cycle checks apply to the planned batch.

`selectCollectionTheme` changes the inspector's collection preview. `setLayerTheme` changes the evaluated layer theme and inheritance below that layer. `clearLayerTheme` restores inheritance. Without an explicit layer theme, the collection's default theme controls evaluated canvas values. Changing an inspector preview alone does not mean the canvas switched theme.

Use the actual `get_session.bindings` descriptor for each `target.kind`, variable type and `location.property`. Binding targets include eligible layers and appropriate style resources; examples of advertised locations include:

| Property family | Variable types / qualifier |
| --- | --- |
| `opacity`, width/height/min/max sizes, side thickness | `float`; eligible layer. |
| Corner radius properties | `float`; corner-radius-capable layer. |
| Padding and horizontal/vertical spacing | `float`; auto-layout layer. |
| `visibility` | `bool`; eligible layer. |
| `text` | `text` or `float`; text layer. |
| `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `paragraphSpacing` | `float`; text layer/style, with supported ranges. |
| `fontFamily` | `text`; text layer/style, with supported ranges. |
| `fontStyle` | `text` or `float`; text layer/style, with supported ranges. |
| `fontVariations` | `float`; indexed font axis and supported range. |
| `fills.color`, `borders.color`, `tint.color` | `color`; appropriate indexed paint and target. |
| `fills.stops.color`, `borders.stops.color` | `color`; paint index plus gradient stop index; ranges only where advertised. |
| Shadow/inner-shadow `.color`, `.radius`, `.x`, `.y`, `.spread` | Color or float as appropriate; indexed effect on eligible layer/effect style. |
| `blur.radius` and advertised glass-effect properties | `float`; eligible layer/effect style. |
| `guides.size`, `.offset`, `.count`, `.gutter`, `.width`, `.height` | `float`; indexed native guide on frame/guide style. |
| `background.color` | `color`; ordinary slice. |

Not every location is valid on every target. Generated properties require a representable native override: scalar/selective paint bindings preserve unrelated inheritance; ranged generated text, selective gradient-stop/numeric-effect/guide edits can require an existing full override. Generated slice bindings are unsupported. Ordinary fields inherited from a linked style require detaching that style explicitly or editing its source first.

Unbinding preserves the current effective or cached value in the target's theme context; it does not resolve a dead variable. Native zero sentinels remain valid, such as automatic line height and unbounded maximum width/height. Deletion follows native dead-reference/save behavior, without a separate API persistence policy.

### Pages and document lifecycle

Page actions are ordered and undoable. Default delete policy is `rejectIfNotEmpty`; explicit `deleteContents` still preserves the last page and components-page roles. A duplication can specify a name/index and preserves relevant content/source ownership through native copy behavior. Page navigation uses `activate_page`; listing does not load every tab.

A loaded document close always carries the current handle/revision, even for `ifUnsaved:"fail"`. `ifUnsaved:"save"` and `"discard"` are explicit decisions; unloaded/failed tabs support only the documented metadata close path. An ungranted local path can return `PermissionDenied`; a plugin does not bypass native file access. User-granted normal open/save flows can authorize the needed destination. `allowDialog` defaults to false.

Local save completion identifies the actual destination and saved revision. Imported source identity and native save destination can differ. Cloud results distinguish actual native pending/sent synchronization state; a clean flag or queued save alone is not proof of server durability. Read the complete result before closing or claiming persistence.

### Libraries

Available/connected library data uses the current authorized account and its existing endpoint connections. The API does not sign in, publish, create a new connection model or grant edit access to a borrowed source. Persistent connect/disconnect operations require an editable cloud target. A local target can discover/import available sources, but its connected list is empty.

Use a locator discovered by `list_libraries`; `kind:"cloud"` is the supported connection kind. An optional `endpoint` must match the discovered source/connection pair, not an arbitrary URL. A document cannot connect to itself. Connecting does not publish. Disconnecting preserves consumers and imported definitions.

A metadata `version:null` is not an import token. An explicit source asset query opens the authorized source and returns its semantic `sourceVersion`. Import uses that token, complete source references, target revision and a fresh request ID. The source library identity plus source asset ID determines reuse; names do not. Import prepares nested components/state owners, styles, aliases, collections/themes and image dependencies before target registration. Repeated unchanged import is a no-op. A new asset does not refresh an already imported dependency; refresh explicitly.

Source access/version, account/endpoint identity, target lifetime/editability and revision are rechecked after asynchronous preparation and immediately before local commit. Refresh is atomic per library, not one global network transaction. Earlier completed items remain completed if a later one fails. Removed source assets are not automatically deleted locally. Inspect each refresh item's `error`, `observedVersion`, `appliedVersion` and `changed` fields.

The server connection request is the association commit point. Cancellation or revision changes after it do not trigger a compensating disconnect. An uncertain network response needs relationship/status inspection before a new request ID. Cleanup after a successful local import/refresh is reported as warnings rather than masking the committed result as a failure.

## Successful data shapes

These shapes are inside `data`, alongside the envelope's available target/revision metadata. Optional or irrelevant fields can be absent/null. An item-level error can coexist with a successful outer read/refresh result.

### Session data

| Field | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| `apiVersion` | `"2"` |
| `sessionId` | Opaque running session ID. |
| `activeTabId`, `activeDocumentHandle` | Optional current navigation metadata. |
| `limits` | Named numeric budgets; see below. |
| `operations` | Array of `{tool, actions: string[], description}` using underlying HTTP operation names. |
| `bindings` | Array of `{property, variableTypes: string[], targetKinds: string[], supportsIndex, supportsRange}`. |

### DocumentInfo and save state

`DocumentInfo` contains `tabId`, optional `documentHandle`, `documentId`, `versionId`, `revision`, `name`, `state`, `isActive`, `canRead`, `canEdit`, `canSave`, and `save`.

`save` contains `kind` (local/cloud context), optional `destination` and `sourcePath`, `isDirty`, `hasPendingChanges`, and `synchronization`. Read the returned native state instead of inferring durable completion from one flag. A tab can be unloaded or failed and have no live readable handle.

`DocumentResult` contains relevant optional `document`, `initialPageId`, `activePageId`, `savedRevision`, `destination`, `closed`, and `tabIds`. Creation returns the ready document and initial page; saves report destination/saved revision; close reports `closed`; reordering reports the actual order.

`PageInfo` is `{id, name, order, isSelected, isComponentsPage}`.

### BatchResult

```json
{
  "created":["<id>"],
  "updated":[],
  "deleted":[],
  "clientIds":{"brand":"<id>"},
  "changed":true,
  "validatedOnly":false
}
```

Validation predictions are not live resource IDs. A meaningful ordered batch can commit even when an early creation is later deleted; a true equal-value no-op does not create history.

### AssetSummary, definition and usage

`AssetSummary` contains `asset` (complete typed reference), `name`, optional `layerId`, `componentId`, `styleType`, `variableType`, `collectionId`, `sourceVersion`, and `supportedActions`.

`AssetDetail` is `{asset, definition?, error?}`. Its definition contains `summary` and the applicable `variable`, `collection`, `theme`, `component`, or `style` payload:

| Definition | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| Variable | `type`, `collectionId`, `values:[{themeId,value}]`, where value is a literal or alias union. |
| Collection | `defaultThemeId`, `selectedThemeId`, `themes:[{id,name,collectionId}]`. |
| Theme | `id`, `name`, `collectionId`. |
| Component | `layerId`, `componentId`, optional `pageId`, `properties`, `stateIds`, optional `stateGroupId`, `defaultStateId`, `states`, optional bounded FREE `content`. |
| Component property | `id`, `name`, `type`, `initialValue`, optional `allowedValues`, `initialVariable`. |
| Component state | `layerId`, `componentId`, `name`, `isDefault`, and dimension `values` dictionary. |
| Style | FREE appearance JSON for the native style kind. |

`AssetUsage` contains `consumerKind`, `consumerId`, optional `layerId`, `pageId`, `name`, `location`, `isInherited`, optional `sourceLayerId`, `themeId`, and `propertyId`. Location uses the same property/index/stop/range coordinates as binding requests. Treat inherited consumers as context, not new independent definitions.

### LayerContext

Each context contains `layerId`, `name`, `type`, optional `pageId`, asset references, `bindings`, `propertyBindings`, `instanceProperties`, effective `themes` dictionary and `warnings`.

- Resolved variable binding: `{location, variable, themeId?, effectiveValue, isOverride}`.
- Component source binding: `{componentId, propertyId, location, effectiveValue, isOverride, storedVariable?}`.
- Instance property: `{componentId, propertyId, name, type, value, isOverride, storedVariable?}`.

The accompanying top-level `assets` array contains definitions used by those layers. Effective values and stored bindings are different facts; an unresolved/dead binding can produce a warning.

### Library data

| Shape | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `LibraryInfo` | `locator`, `name`, `state`, `canRead`, `isConnected`, optional `version`. State distinguishes native connected/disconnected/loading/failed/inaccessible conditions. |
| `AssetMapping` | `{source: AssetReference, local: AssetReference}`. |
| Import result | `assets` mappings, `changes: BatchResult`, applied `sourceVersion`. |
| `LibraryRefreshItem` | `libraryId`, `observedVersion`, optional `appliedVersion`, `changed`, optional `error`. |

### Status and documentation

`get_request_status` data is `{status, result?}`; `result` is the original retained envelope for a completed request. `get_automation_documentation` data is `{topic, content}` with focused text.

## Limits and recovery budgets

| Budget | Current limit |
| --- | --- |
| Default/max paged results | 50 / 200 |
| Detail references / changes / explicit import or refresh entries | 100 each |
| Typed HTTP request JSON | 2 MiB |
| Discovery response data | 2 MiB |
| Replay entries / completed bytes / retention | 256 / 16 MiB / one hour |
| Component inspection | Depth 8, 4,096 nodes |
| Layer context | 100 roots, 4,096 visited nodes and bindings |
| Prepared text | 1,000 text layers, 1,000,000 aggregate UTF-16 characters |
| Prepared component graph | 1,024 components, depth 128, 8 layout passes |
| Variable consumers | 1,000,000 candidates, 10,000 consumer layers |
| Library source reads | At most 8 explicit libraries; at most 2 native metadata pages per available-list request |
| Library source fingerprint serialization | 16 MiB plus graph/value work bounds |
| Prepared library images | 4,096 unique images; 16 MiB aggregate encoded input; 16,777,216 decoded pixels; 30-second window |

The running session is authoritative for advertised limits; additional bounded graph/depth/layout work checks can reject a complex request. `LimitExceeded` means reduce the actual work, not only the number of top-level changes. Keep retries bounded and preserve already completed per-library outcomes. Legacy image upload retains its separate 200 MiB binary budget; it is not a typed v2 import request.

## Legacy targeting and format boundary

Legacy endpoints keep their original raw array/string/wrapper request bodies and response forms. `X-Lunacy-Document-Handle` can explicitly target applicable legacy document routes. Use `X-Lunacy-Page-Id` only for page-scoped reads/placement/captures, such as viewport/area, new layers/SVG and image insertion. Unsupported or contradictory headers fail. Do not place these headers in a shared client's mutable defaults when requests can run concurrently; add them to each request. V2 requests carry selectors in their JSON bodies.

The saved `.free` document contract is maintained in [icons8/free](https://github.com/icons8/free). API envelopes, handles, revisions, replay entries, chat history and internal undo records are not public FREE archive fields. Matching preview builds may write FREE metadata version 12 to retain generated border/effect/text/guide style links; the published upstream main specification can still describe an earlier version. Consult the published [README/changelog](https://github.com/icons8/free/blob/main/README.md) for that normative release and the separately labeled [FREE 12 proposal](https://github.com/icons8/free/pull/4) for pending additions. Do not present the proposal as merged or assume an older reader preserves new links on resave.


# Plugin API reference
Source: https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/raw/plugin-api.md

Complete legacy HTTP, WebSocket event and plugin UI contracts

This complete reference is synchronized from the [lunacy-plugins article](https://github.com/icons8/lunacy-plugins/blob/7b82b78118e2c66a474f3d556b171903af12bcbc/docs/API_REFERENCE.md) at commit `7b82b781`, checked on November 5, 2026. See [Plugins](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugins/) for installation and manifests.

This page documents the legacy layer/image/export API and plugin WebSocket/UI contracts. The new document, component, style, variable and library operations have a separate [Automation API v2 reference](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-v2/), [complete request schemas](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-schemas/), and [worked workflows](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-workflows/).

The v2 additions require a matching preview build. Probe `/v2/get_session`; do not assume a published release contains every documented operation. Existing plugin process, manifest, event and UI contracts continue to apply.

## Connection and response formats

The default HTTP address is `http://localhost:31415`. The plugin WebSocket server starts at `ws://localhost:31416`. Each server can choose a later available port independently; use the running application's actual ports. An installed valid plugin starts the local automation service automatically. For standalone development, **AI → Model Context Protocol → MCP server enabled** can enable it without a plugin. See the [development guide](https://github.com/icons8/lunacy-plugins/blob/7b82b78118e2c66a474f3d556b171903af12bcbc/docs/PLUGIN_DEVELOPMENT_GUIDE.md) for manifests and lifecycle modes.

Legacy endpoints return different formats: FREE JSON text, plain text, structured JSON, SVG or binary bytes. There is no universal legacy success/error envelope. Many string-based tools return a plain-text operation failure even with HTTP 200. Inspect the documented body as well as status. JSON text may arrive with `text/plain`; do not assume `response.json()` works for every endpoint. UI operations have their own `success` property; only `/v2/*` uses the v2 `ok` envelope.

Use `application/json` for JSON bodies, except the plain-text undo count and binary image upload below. Layer/asset IDs are opaque. Preserve the spelling and identity kind returned by the relevant route.

## Explicit document targets

On a matching v2 build, discover `documentHandle` with `/v2/list_documents`. For legacy routes supporting explicit document/page targeting, pass these headers on the individual request:

```http
X-Lunacy-Document-Handle: <live-document-handle>
X-Lunacy-Page-Id: <page-id>
```

The page header further qualifies an eligible request; it is not navigation. A page must belong to the target document. Viewport/selection operations retain native constraints. Unsupported header/route combinations are rejected. Do not silently retry against the active tab or put changing targets in shared global client headers. Older builds without these additions retain active-document behavior.

These headers do not give legacy writes v2 request IDs, revision guards or replay semantics. Use the corresponding v2 operation when those guarantees are needed. A stale/closed/read-only/unavailable target fails explicitly. See the [workflow example](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-workflows/#combine-v2-with-legacy-layer-export-and-ui-calls).

## Layer and viewport reads

| Route | Body | Successful body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /getselected` | None | FREE object for one selected layer, array for multiple, `{}` for no selection. |
| `POST /getlayersbyids` | JSON array of layer ID strings. | FREE object/array; a missing target can return text. |
| `POST /getcomponents` | JSON array of component ID strings. | Matching source definitions as FREE object/array; `{}` when none. Not an unfiltered catalog query. |
| `POST /getlayersinarea` | `{x,y,width,height,maxDepth?}`. | FREE layer data in the canvas rectangle. `maxDepth` defaults to `1`. |
| `POST /getlayersdata` | `{layerIds:[...]}`. | SVG with layer metadata. This route uses full GUID layer IDs. |
| `GET /getviewportinfo` | None | Text: `Viewport: x=..., y=..., width=..., height=...`. |

Coordinates use native canvas space; area fields are integers. Exported layers follow the [public FREE specification](https://github.com/icons8/free/blob/main/README.md). Handle object/array/empty cases rather than assuming every result is an array.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:31415/getlayersbyids \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '["<returned-layer-id>"]'
```

For reusable-asset search and complete component definitions, prefer `/v2/query_design_system` then `/v2/get_design_system_assets`. These distinguish component IDs from source-layer IDs and include individual asset errors.

## Layer writes

| Route | Body | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /setselected` | Direct FREE object or array. | Edits/replaces supplied existing selected layers. Requires a nonempty current selection and IDs belonging to it. Does not select arbitrary IDs; `[]` does not clear selection. |
| `POST /updatelayers` | Direct FREE object or array. | Updates existing layers by their IDs. |
| `POST /createlayers` | `{layersJson:"<serialized FREE JSON>",parentId?}`. | Creates content under an eligible parent, or native page root when omitted. |
| `POST /createlayersfromsvg` | `{svg:"<svg>...</svg>",x?,y?,parentId?}`. | Creates from SVG; `x` and `y` default to `0`. |
| `POST /updatelayerfromsvg` | `{layerId,svg}`. | Updates eligible layer content through native SVG import. |
| `POST /deletelayers` | JSON array of layer ID strings. | Deletes the specified eligible layers. |
| `POST /duplicatelayers` | `{layerIds:[...],offsetX?,offsetY?,componentsToInstances?}`. | Duplicates layers; offsets default to `10`, component-to-instance conversion to `true`. |

Except duplication, these writes return native success/error text. Duplication returns `{duplicatedLayerIds:[...],message:"..."}`; inspect IDs and message. It can return no duplicated IDs on failure. Native editability, generated-node, resource and parent constraints still apply.

For `/setselected` and `/updatelayers`, send the layer JSON directly:

```json
[{"_t":"RECT","id":"<existing-layer-id>","name":"Updated shape"}]
```

Only `/createlayers` uses `layersJson`, whose value is a **string**, not an array:

```json
{
  "parentId": "<frame-layer-id>",
  "layersJson": "[{\"_t\":\"RECT\",\"name\":\"New shape\",\"size\":[120,80],\"fill\":\"0A84FF\"}]"
}
```

Read exported content and the normative [FREE specification](https://github.com/icons8/free) for property types, transforms and ID encodings. Layer APIs cannot bypass typed v2 rules for imported definitions, aliases, styles or component properties.

## Images and screenshots

| Route | Body | Successful body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /getimage` | `{imageId,format?}`. | Image bytes with `Content-Type`; missing image returns 404. |
| `POST /getscreenshotbyid` | JSON array of layer ID strings. | Binary screenshot. |
| `POST /getscreenshotviewport` | None. | Binary screenshot of an eligible current viewport. |
| `POST /getscreenshotarea` | `{x,y,width,height}`. | Binary screenshot of the canvas rectangle. |
| `POST /insertimage` | Raw image bytes, not JSON/base64. | Native insertion result text. |

Screenshot response headers, when applicable:

| Header | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `X-Screenshot-AbsoluteX`, `X-Screenshot-AbsoluteY` | Canvas-space origin. |
| `X-Screenshot-Width`, `X-Screenshot-Height` | Dimensions. |
| `X-Screenshot-Timestamp` | Capture timestamp. |
| `X-Screenshot-Error` | Failure description. |

Inspect status, error header and `Content-Type` before treating a response as image bytes:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:31415/getscreenshotarea \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"x":0,"y":0,"width":640,"height":480}' --output screenshot.png
```

Image upload headers:

| Header | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `X-Image-Position-X`, `X-Image-Position-Y` | Insertion coordinates. |
| `X-Image-File-Name` | Filename, including extension. |
| `X-Image-Parent-Id` | Optional eligible parent ID. |

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:31415/insertimage \
  -H 'Content-Type: image/png' \
  -H 'X-Image-Position-X: 40' -H 'X-Image-Position-Y: 40' \
  -H 'X-Image-File-Name: picture.png' --data-binary @picture.png
```

Legacy image upload has a 200 MiB limit. Native decoding/access rules still apply. This is separate from v2 prepared-library-image budgets.

## Export

`POST /export` fields:

| Field | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `layerIds` | Array of explicit layer ID strings. | Supply targets. |
| `format` | String: `PNG`, `SVG`, `PDF`, `JPG`, `WEBP`, `TIFF`, `ICO`. | `PNG`. |
| `scale` | Number. | `1`. |
| `mergeObjects` | Boolean. | `false`. |

The response is an array of `{layerId,fileName,contentType,data}`. `data` is a **base64 string** containing file bytes, not an array of integers:

```javascript
const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/export`, {
  method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ layerIds, format: 'PNG', scale: 1, mergeObjects: false })
});
if (!response.ok) {
  throw new Error(`Export failed: HTTP ${response.status}`);
}
const results = await response.json();
for (const result of results) {
  const bytes = Buffer.from(result.data, 'base64');
  console.log(result.fileName, result.contentType, bytes.length);
}
```

This Node.js 18+ fragment assumes previously defined `baseUrl`/`layerIds`. Validate/choose an output filename before writing decoded bytes. Export returns data; it does not write a file to a destination supplied in this request.

## Undo, redo and toast notifications

`POST /getundostack` takes a positive integer as a **plain-text body**, for example `20`, and returns native history text. It is not GET and does not take a JSON options object. `POST /undo` and `POST /redo` take no body and return text.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:31415/getundostack -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' --data '20'
```

`POST /showtoast` fields:

| Field | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | String. | Supply a message. |
| `iconType` | Byte. | `0`. |
| `priority` | Byte. | `5`. |
| `durationSeconds` | 16-bit integer. | `7`. |
| `isContinuable` | Boolean. | `true`. |
| `isSkippable` | Boolean. | `false`. |
| `isAttention` | Boolean. | `false`. |

Icons: `0` None, `1` Copy, `2` CheckDone, `3` Document, `4` Warning, `5` Update, `6` Love, `7` Human, `8` Trash, `9` Smile, `10` CloudDisconnect, `11` Message, `12` Copyright, `13` Stars. A success/check toast uses `2`.

```json
{"text":"Plugin finished","iconType":2,"durationSeconds":4}
```

## Plugin UI HTTP API

All four routes use POST. UI values are strings, including checkbox/number/slider values; parse them explicitly.

| Route | JSON body | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/registerui` | `{pluginId,title,fields:[...]}`. | `{success:true,message:"UI registered successfully"}`. |
| `/getpluginuivalues` | JSON string, e.g. `"my-plugin"`. | Object mapping field IDs to strings, or `{}`. |
| `/unregisterui` | JSON string, e.g. `"my-plugin"`. | `{success,message}`; false when not found. |
| `/updateuifields` | `{pluginId,updates:{fieldId:"value"}}`. | `{success,message}`; inspect `success` for unknown UI/empty updates. |

Fields support `id`, `type`, `label`, and optional `description`, `placeholder`, `value`, `options`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `multiline`. Values/options are strings; min/max/step are numbers; multiline is boolean. Canonical field types: `text`, `number`, `select`, `checkbox`, `separator`, `button`, `slider`, `linkButton`, `label`.

```json
{
  "pluginId":"my-plugin","title":"Export helper",
  "fields":[
    {"id":"scale","type":"number","label":"Scale","value":"1","min":0.1,"max":4,"step":0.1},
    {"id":"export","type":"button","label":"Export"}
  ]
}
```

Register after the WebSocket `plugin_initialized` handshake and repeat after reconnecting. See the [UI tutorial](https://github.com/icons8/lunacy-plugins/blob/7b82b78118e2c66a474f3d556b171903af12bcbc/docs/QUICK_START_UI.md), [UI guide](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-ui/), and [service example](https://github.com/icons8/lunacy-plugins/tree/7b82b78118e2c66a474f3d556b171903af12bcbc/featured-plugins/bitmap-to-vector-plugin).

## WebSocket events

Declare required event groups in the manifest's `events` array. Use service mode for background listeners. Connect to the actual WebSocket port and identify the plugin:

```json
{"type":"plugin_register","pluginId":"my-plugin"}
```

Wait for `plugin_initialized` before registering UI. Reconnect with bounded backoff, identify/register again, and rebuild cached state. Events include `type` and UTC `timestamp`; optional fields can be absent/null. UI messages use camelCase fields. The older selection/undo/document/window fields use the explicit snake_case names below.

### Selection

```json
{
  "type":"selection","timestamp":"2026-11-05T10:00:00Z",
  "selected_layers":[{"id":"<layer-id>","name":"Button"}]
}
```

`selected_layers` is an array of `{id,name}`; it is empty when selection clears. There are no `layer_ids` or `layer_count` fields. Read full layer data through HTTP when needed.

### Undo/history

```json
{
  "type":"undo","timestamp":"2026-11-05T10:00:00Z","operation_type":"created",
  "operation_description":"<native-operation-name>",
  "affected_layers":[{"id":"<layer-id>","name":"Button","type":"<native-layer-type>"}]
}
```

`operation_type` is `created`, `undo`, or `redo`. Description/layers are optional; non-layer operations need not supply layer entries. Native operation/layer descriptions are descriptive values, not a stable command vocabulary.

### Documents

```json
{
  "type":"document","timestamp":"2026-11-05T10:00:00Z","document_type":"activated",
  "document_id":"<persisted-document-id>","document_name":"Design","document_path":null
}
```

`document_type` can be `opening`, `opened`, `closing`, `closed`, `activated`, `deactivated`. ID/name/path are optional. Persisted `document_id` is not a v2 live handle; reread `/v2/list_documents` before targeting. Events do not replace revision/status checks.

### Window

```json
{"type":"window","timestamp":"2026-11-05T10:00:00Z","event_type":"focused"}
```

`event_type`: `focused`, `unfocused`, `state_changed`, `closing`. State changes can include `window_state` with the native state name.

### UI events

`plugin_initialized` contains the common event fields. `show_ui` and `close_ui` also include `pluginId`. Field events identify a field and its string value:

```json
{
  "type":"ui_field_event","timestamp":"2026-11-05T10:00:00Z",
  "pluginId":"my-plugin","fieldId":"scale","eventType":"value_change","value":"2"
}
```

`eventType` is `value_change` or `click`; `value` may be absent/null for a button. Filter by your plugin ID. UI show/close messages are distinct from document lifecycle events.

## Errors and work budgets

HTTP 400 indicates invalid HTTP/JSON input, 404 an unavailable route/resource, 405 an unsupported method, 500 an unexpected error. Explicit-target failures can also return 403/409 and text beginning with a stable automation error code. Preserve status/body for diagnosis. Do not assume a v2 `{ok,error}` envelope or universal legacy `{error,message,code}` object.

Native work, decoding, export, plugin command timeouts and v2 request/model limits have separate budgets. There is no promise of unlimited work or a fixed requests-per-second quota. Batch reads, debounce events, avoid overlapping writes and inspect `/v2/get_session.data.limits` where supported.

## FREE data and version compatibility

The saved/exported `.free` archive contract is maintained in [icons8/free](https://github.com/icons8/free), with its normative [specification/changelog](https://github.com/icons8/free/blob/main/README.md). Read exported values instead of guessing geometry/color encodings.

Matching preview builds may write FREE version 12 for extra generated style links. Its [upstream proposal](https://github.com/icons8/free/pull/4) is pending separately from published `main`; do not assume an older release preserves those links. HTTP envelopes, handles, revisions, replay, internal history and chat state are not public FREE document fields.


# Plugin UI guide
Source: https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/raw/plugin-ui.md

Build plugin dialogs with native fields, values and lifecycle events

This complete reference is synchronized from the [lunacy-plugins article](https://github.com/icons8/lunacy-plugins/blob/7b82b78118e2c66a474f3d556b171903af12bcbc/docs/PLUGIN_UI_GUIDE.md) at commit `7b82b781`, checked on November 5, 2026. See [Plugins](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugins/) for installation and manifests.

Complete guide to creating user interfaces for Lunacy plugins, including toast notifications,
dynamic UI forms, and external applications.

The UI protocol remains compatible with the new preview [Automation API v2](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-v2/).
Use its [workflows](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-workflows/) for document, component, style and variable
operations behind your UI. The [legacy reference](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api/#plugin-ui-http-api)
summarizes exact UI request/response and event shapes. UI values are strings; check
the `success` property of UI responses as well as HTTP status, and re-register after
each WebSocket handshake/reconnect.

## Toast Notifications

Display status messages inside Lunacy without creating a full UI dialog.

### Basic Usage

```javascript
await axios.post('http://localhost:31415/showtoast', {
  text: 'Export complete!',
  iconType: 2
});
```

### Icon Types

| Type | Icon | Use Case |
|------|------|----------|
| 0 | None | Neutral message |
| 1 | Copy | Copy operation |
| 2 | CheckDone | Completed successfully |
| 3 | Document | Document-related |
| 4 | Warning | Warning/Error |
| 5 | Update | Loading/In progress |
| 6 | Love | Favorites/Like |
| 7 | Human | User-related |
| 8 | Trash | Delete operation |
| 9 | Smile | Positive feedback |
| 10 | CloudDisconnect | Sync/Connection issues |
| 11 | Message | Notifications |
| 12 | Copyright | License/Copyright |
| 13 | Stars | Featured/Special |

### Toast Options

```javascript
await axios.post('http://localhost:31415/showtoast', {
  text: 'Processing...',
  iconType: 5,
  priority: 5,
  durationSeconds: 7,
  isContinuable: true,
  isSkippable: false,
  isAttention: false
});
```

**Fields:**

- `text` (string, required) - Message to display
- `iconType` (number) - Icon type from table above (default: 0)
- `priority` (number) - Priority level, higher shows first (default: 5)
- `durationSeconds` (number) - Display duration in seconds (default: 7)
- `isContinuable` (boolean) - Can be paused on hover (default: true)
- `isSkippable` (boolean) - Can be skipped by newer toasts (default: false)
- `isAttention` (boolean) - Attention-grabbing toast (default: false)

### Progress Updates

Show progress during long operations:

```javascript
for (let i = 0; i < layers.length; i++) {
  await axios.post('http://localhost:31415/showtoast', {
    text: `Processing ${i + 1} of ${layers.length}...`,
    iconType: 5,
    isContinuable: true
  });
  await processLayer(layers[i]);
}

await axios.post('http://localhost:31415/showtoast', {
  text: 'Complete!',
  iconType: 2
});
```

---

## Dynamic UI System

Plugin registers UI definition via API, Lunacy renders interactive dialog.

### Overview

**Architecture:**

```
Plugin → POST /registerui → Lunacy displays dialog
Plugin ← WebSocket events ← User interacts with UI
Plugin → POST /getpluginuivalues → Get user input
Plugin → POST /unregisterui → Close dialog
```

**Key Components:**

- **Service plugins** - MUST use WebSocket for UI lifecycle events
- **Utility plugins** - Can use WebSocket or polling (WebSocket recommended)
- **Field types** - 9 field types available (text, number, slider, etc.)
- **Events** - Real-time notifications when UI is opened/closed/interacted

---

## Lifecycle

```
┌──────────────┐                    ┌──────────────┐
│   Plugin     │                    │   Lunacy     │
└──────┬───────┘                    └──────┬───────┘
       │                                   │
       │ 1. WebSocket connect              │
       ├──────────────────────────────────►│
       │                                   │
       │ 2. plugin_register                │
       ├──────────────────────────────────►│
       │                                   │
       │ 3. plugin_initialized             │
       │◄──────────────────────────────────┤
       │                                   │
       │ 4. POST /registerui               │
       ├──────────────────────────────────►│
       │                                   │ UI registered
       │                           User opens plugin UI
       │                                   │
       │ 5. show_ui event                  │
       │◄──────────────────────────────────┤
       │                                   │
       │ (optional) POST /updateuifields   │
       ├──────────────────────────────────►│
       │                                   │ Fields updated
       │                           User clicks Apply/OK
       │                                   │
       │ 6. ui_field_event (click)         │
       │◄──────────────────────────────────┤
       │                                   │
       │ 7. POST /getpluginuivalues        │
       ├──────────────────────────────────►│
       │                                   │
       │ { field values }                  │
       │◄──────────────────────────────────┤
       │                                   │
       │ 8. Process values                 │
       │                           User closes dialog
       │                                   │
       │ 9. close_ui event                 │
       │◄──────────────────────────────────┤
       │                                   │
       │ 10. POST /unregisterui            │
       ├──────────────────────────────────►│
       │                                   │ UI closed
```

**Important Notes:**

1. **Register UI only AFTER `plugin_initialized` event**
2. **Always unregister UI** when done (cleanup)
3. **Listen to `show_ui`/`close_ui` events** for proper lifecycle handling
4. **Parse all values** - they come as strings

---

## API Endpoints

### POST /registerui

Register plugin UI definition.

**Request:**

```json
{
  "pluginId": "my-plugin",
  "title": "Plugin Settings",
  "fields": [
    {
      "id": "format",
      "type": "select",
      "label": "Format",
      "value": "PNG",
      "options": ["PNG", "JPEG", "SVG"],
      "description": "Export format"
    },
    {
      "id": "quality",
      "type": "slider",
      "label": "Quality",
      "value": "80",
      "min": 0,
      "max": 100,
      "step": 5,
      "description": "Export quality (0-100%)"
    }
  ]
}
```

**Response:** `200 OK` with `{"success":true,"message":"UI registered successfully"}`.

### POST /getpluginuivalues

Retrieve current field values from UI.

**Request Body:**

```json
"my-plugin"
```

**Response:**

```json
{
  "format": "PNG",
  "quality": "80"
}
```

**Note:** All values returned as strings - parse numbers/booleans!

### POST /updateuifields

Update field values programmatically while UI is open.

**Request:**

```json
{
  "pluginId": "my-plugin",
  "updates": {
    "format": "JPEG",
    "quality": "95"
  }
}
```

**Response:**

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "UI fields updated successfully"
}
```

**Use Cases:**

- Apply presets (change all fields at once)
- Sync dependent fields automatically
- Reset preset to "Custom" when user changes value
- Calculate optimal values based on selection

### POST /unregisterui

Clean up and close UI.

**Request:**

```json
"my-plugin"
```

**Response:** `200 OK` with a `success`/`message` object. `success:false` means the plugin UI was not found.

---

## WebSocket Events

### Connection

```javascript
const ws = new WebSocket('ws://localhost:31416');
```

### Plugin Registration

**Send after connecting (required):**

```json
{
  "type": "plugin_register",
  "pluginId": "my-plugin"
}
```

**Lunacy responds with:**

```json
{
  "type": "plugin_initialized",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-20T12:34:56.789Z"
}
```

**⚠️ CRITICAL:** Only call `/registerui` AFTER receiving `plugin_initialized`!

### UI Lifecycle Events

**show_ui** - Dialog opened by user:

```json
{
  "type": "show_ui",
  "pluginId": "my-plugin",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-20T12:34:56.789Z"
}
```

**close_ui** - Dialog closed by user:

```json
{
  "type": "close_ui",
  "pluginId": "my-plugin",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-20T12:34:56.789Z"
}
```

**ui_field_event** - User interacted with field:

Button click:

```json
{
  "type": "ui_field_event",
  "pluginId": "my-plugin",
  "fieldId": "apply",
  "eventType": "click",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-20T12:34:56.789Z"
}
```

Value change:

```json
{
  "type": "ui_field_event",
  "pluginId": "my-plugin",
  "fieldId": "preset",
  "eventType": "value_change",
  "value": "High Quality",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-20T12:34:56.789Z"
}
```

**Event Types:**

- `"click"` - Button clicks
- `"value_change"` - Field value changes (text, number, slider, checkbox, select)

---

## Field Types

### text

Single-line or multi-line text input.

```json
{
  "id": "filename",
  "type": "text",
  "label": "File Name",
  "value": "export",
  "placeholder": "Enter file name",
  "description": "Output file name without extension",
  "multiline": false
}
```

**Properties:**

- `id` (string, required)
- `type` = "text"
- `label` (string, required)
- `value` (string) - Initial value
- `placeholder` (string) - Placeholder text
- `description` (string) - Tooltip on hover
- `multiline` (boolean) - Enable textarea (default: false)

**Returns:** String

---

### number

Numeric input with constraints, supports math expressions.

```json
{
  "id": "count",
  "type": "number",
  "label": "Count",
  "value": "10",
  "min": 1,
  "max": 100,
  "step": 1,
  "description": "Number of copies"
}
```

**Properties:**

- `id` (string, required)
- `type` = "number"
- `label` (string, required)
- `value` (string) - Initial value as string
- `min` (number) - Minimum value
- `max` (number) - Maximum value
- `step` (number) - Increment step
- `description` (string) - Tooltip on hover

**Features:**

- Supports decimal precision (up to 10 places)
- Allows math expressions: "10*2", "50/4"
- Enforces min/max boundaries

**Returns:** String (parse with `parseInt()` or `parseFloat()`)

**When to use:** Exact numeric input without visual feedback needed.

---

### slider

Combined slider + numeric input for visual parameter adjustment.

```json
{
  "id": "opacity",
  "type": "slider",
  "label": "Opacity",
  "value": "100",
  "min": 0,
  "max": 100,
  "step": 5,
  "description": "Layer opacity (0-100%)"
}
```

**Properties:**

- `id` (string, required)
- `type` = "slider"
- `label` (string, required)
- `value` (string) - Initial value as string
- `min` (number, required) - Minimum value
- `max` (number, required) - Maximum value
- `step` (number) - Increment step
- `description` (string) - Tooltip on hover

**Behavior:**

- Dual control: Slider (left) + NumericBox (right)
- Both controls stay synchronized
- Slider provides visual feedback
- NumericBox allows precise input with math expressions

**Returns:** String (parse with `parseFloat()`)

**When to use:** Parameters that benefit from visual feedback (opacity, thresholds, quality).

---

### checkbox

Boolean checkbox.

```json
{
  "id": "includeHidden",
  "type": "checkbox",
  "label": "Include Hidden Layers",
  "value": "false",
  "description": "Process hidden layers"
}
```

**Properties:**

- `id` (string, required)
- `type` = "checkbox"
- `label` (string, required)
- `value` (string) - "true" or "false"
- `description` (string) - Tooltip on hover

**Returns:** String "true" or "false" (check with `=== 'true'`)

---

### select

Dropdown menu with predefined options.

```json
{
  "id": "format",
  "type": "select",
  "label": "Format",
  "value": "PNG",
  "options": ["PNG", "JPEG", "SVG", "PDF"],
  "description": "Export format"
}
```

**Properties:**

- `id` (string, required)
- `type` = "select"
- `label` (string, required)
- `value` (string) - Initially selected option
- `options` (`string[]`, required) - Available options
- `description` (string) - Tooltip on hover

**Returns:** String (selected option)

---

### button

Clickable button that sends events.

```json
{
  "id": "apply",
  "type": "button",
  "label": "Apply Changes",
  "description": "Apply settings and close"
}
```

**Properties:**

- `id` (string, required)
- `type` = "button"
- `label` (string, required) - Button text
- `description` (string) - Tooltip on hover

**Behavior:** On click → sends `ui_field_event` with `eventType: "click"`

**No return value** - listen for WebSocket event

---

### linkButton

Hyperlink-styled button that opens URLs.

```json
{
  "id": "docs",
  "type": "linkButton",
  "label": "View Documentation",
  "value": "https://github.com/user/plugin#readme",
  "description": "Open plugin documentation"
}
```

**Properties:**

- `id` (string, required)
- `type` = "linkButton"
- `label` (string, required) - Link text
- `value` (string) - URL to open
- `description` (string) - Tooltip on hover

**Behavior:**

- Opens URL in default browser
- No event sent to plugin (handled by Lunacy)
- URL is automatically decoded

**When to use:** Documentation links, repository URLs, donation pages.

---

### label

Read-only static text display.

```json
{
  "type": "label",
  "value": "Plugin v1.2.3 | Engine v0.6.4",
  "description": "Current versions"
}
```

**Properties:**

- `type` = "label"
- `value` (string) - Text to display
- `description` (string) - Tooltip on hover
- `id` not required (not interactive)

**Behavior:**

- Static, non-editable text
- Automatic text wrapping
- Adapts to light/dark theme

**When to use:** Version info, warnings, descriptions, static context.

**Multi-line example:**

```json
{
  "type": "label",
  "value": "⚠️ High precision settings may take longer to process.\nRecommended for final output only."
}
```

---

### separator

Visual separator (horizontal line).

```json
{
  "type": "separator",
  "label": "Advanced Options"
}
```

**Properties:**

- `type` = "separator"
- `label` (string, optional) - Section title
- `id` not required

**When to use:** Group related fields visually.

---

## Complete Examples

### Service Plugin with UI (Node.js)

```javascript
const axios = require('axios');
const WebSocket = require('ws');

const API = 'http://localhost:31415';
const WS_URL = 'ws://localhost:31416';
const PLUGIN_ID = 'my-plugin';

let ws;

async function registerUi() {
  await axios.post(`${API}/registerui`, {
    pluginId: PLUGIN_ID,
    title: 'Export Settings',
    fields: [
      {
        id: 'preset',
        type: 'select',
        label: 'Preset',
        value: 'Standard',
        options: ['Draft', 'Standard', 'High Quality'],
        description: 'Quality preset'
      },
      {
        type: 'separator',
        label: 'Export Options'
      },
      {
        id: 'format',
        type: 'select',
        label: 'Format',
        value: 'PNG',
        options: ['PNG', 'JPEG', 'SVG']
      },
      {
        id: 'quality',
        type: 'slider',
        label: 'Quality',
        value: '80',
        min: 0,
        max: 100,
        step: 5
      },
      {
        type: 'separator'
      },
      {
        id: 'apply',
        type: 'button',
        label: 'Export'
      }
    ]
  });
  console.log('✓ UI registered');
}

async function unregisterUi() {
  try {
    await axios.post(`${API}/unregisterui`, PLUGIN_ID);
    console.log('✓ UI unregistered');
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Failed to unregister UI:', error.message);
  }
}

async function getFieldValues() {
  try {
    const response = await axios.post(`${API}/getpluginuivalues`, PLUGIN_ID);
    return response.data;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Failed to get values:', error.message);
    return {};
  }
}

async function applyPreset(presetName) {
  const presets = {
    'Draft': { quality: '50' },
    'Standard': { quality: '80' },
    'High Quality': { quality: '95' }
  };
  
  const preset = presets[presetName];
  if (preset) {
    await axios.post(`${API}/updateuifields`, {
      pluginId: PLUGIN_ID,
      updates: preset
    });
  }
}

async function performExport(values) {
  const format = values.format;
  const quality = parseFloat(values.quality);
  
  console.log(`Exporting as ${format} with quality ${quality}...`);
  
  await axios.post(`${API}/showtoast`, {
    text: `Exporting as ${format}...`,
    iconType: 5
  });
  
  // Export logic here...
  
  await axios.post(`${API}/showtoast`, {
    text: 'Export complete!',
    iconType: 2
  });
}

function onMessage(message) {
  try {
    const event = JSON.parse(message);
    
    if (event.type === 'plugin_initialized') {
      console.log('✓ Plugin initialized');
      registerUi();
    }
    else if (event.type === 'show_ui' && event.pluginId === PLUGIN_ID) {
      console.log('✓ UI opened by user');
    }
    else if (event.type === 'close_ui' && event.pluginId === PLUGIN_ID) {
      console.log('✓ UI closed by user');
    }
    else if (event.type === 'ui_field_event' && event.pluginId === PLUGIN_ID) {
      const fieldId = event.fieldId;
      const eventType = event.eventType;
      
      if (fieldId === 'preset' && eventType === 'value_change') {
        console.log(`Preset changed to: ${event.value}`);
        applyPreset(event.value);
      }
      else if (fieldId === 'apply' && eventType === 'click') {
        console.log('Apply clicked - getting values...');
        getFieldValues().then(values => {
          performExport(values);
        });
      }
    }
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error processing message:', error.message);
  }
}

function start() {
  ws = new WebSocket(WS_URL);
  
  ws.on('open', () => {
    console.log('✓ WebSocket connected');
    ws.send(JSON.stringify({
      type: 'plugin_register',
      pluginId: PLUGIN_ID
    }));
    console.log('✓ Sent plugin registration');
  });
  
  ws.on('message', (data) => {
    onMessage(data.toString());
  });
  
  ws.on('error', (error) => {
    console.error('WebSocket error:', error.message);
  });
  
  ws.on('close', () => {
    console.log('WebSocket closed');
  });
}

process.on('SIGTERM', async () => {
  console.log('Shutting down...');
  await unregisterUi();
  if (ws) ws.close();
  process.exit(0);
});

start();
```

### Service Plugin with UI (Python)

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import requests
import json
import asyncio
import websockets

LUNACY_API = "http://localhost:31415"
LUNACY_WS = "ws://localhost:31416"
PLUGIN_ID = "my-plugin"

def register_ui():
    ui_definition = {
        "pluginId": PLUGIN_ID,
        "title": "Export Settings",
        "fields": [
            {
                "id": "format",
                "type": "select",
                "label": "Format",
                "value": "PNG",
                "options": ["PNG", "JPEG", "SVG"],
                "description": "Export format"
            },
            {
                "id": "quality",
                "type": "slider",
                "label": "Quality",
                "value": "80",
                "min": 0,
                "max": 100,
                "step": 5,
                "description": "Export quality (0-100%)"
            },
            {
                "type": "separator"
            },
            {
                "id": "apply",
                "type": "button",
                "label": "Export"
            }
        ]
    }
    
    try:
        response = requests.post(
            f"{LUNACY_API}/registerui",
            json=ui_definition,
            headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
            timeout=5
        )
        response.raise_for_status()
        print("✓ UI registered")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Failed to register UI: {e}")

def unregister_ui():
    try:
        requests.post(
            f"{LUNACY_API}/unregisterui",
            json=PLUGIN_ID,
            headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
            timeout=5
        )
        print("✓ UI unregistered")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Failed to unregister UI: {e}")

def get_field_values():
    try:
        response = requests.post(
            f"{LUNACY_API}/getpluginuivalues",
            json=PLUGIN_ID,
            headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
            timeout=5
        )
        response.raise_for_status()
        return response.json()
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Failed to get values: {e}")
        return {}

def perform_export(values):
    format_val = values.get('format', 'PNG')
    quality = float(values.get('quality', 80))
    
    print(f"Exporting as {format_val} with quality {quality}...")
    
    requests.post(f"{LUNACY_API}/showtoast", json={
        "text": f"Exporting as {format_val}...",
        "iconType": 5
    })
    
    # Export logic here...
    
    requests.post(f"{LUNACY_API}/showtoast", json={
        "text": "Export complete!",
        "iconType": 2
    })

async def handle_websocket():
    async with websockets.connect(LUNACY_WS) as ws:
        print("✓ WebSocket connected")
        
        await ws.send(json.dumps({
            "type": "plugin_register",
            "pluginId": PLUGIN_ID
        }))
        print("✓ Sent plugin registration")
        
        async for message in ws:
            try:
                event = json.loads(message)
                event_type = event.get('type')
                
                if event_type == 'plugin_initialized':
                    print("✓ Plugin initialized")
                    register_ui()
                
                elif event_type == 'show_ui' and event.get('pluginId') == PLUGIN_ID:
                    print("✓ UI opened by user")
                
                elif event_type == 'close_ui' and event.get('pluginId') == PLUGIN_ID:
                    print("✓ UI closed by user")
                
                elif event_type == 'ui_field_event' and event.get('pluginId') == PLUGIN_ID:
                    field_id = event.get('fieldId')
                    event_type_detail = event.get('eventType')
                    
                    if field_id == 'apply' and event_type_detail == 'click':
                        print("Apply clicked - getting values...")
                        values = get_field_values()
                        perform_export(values)
                        
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Error processing message: {e}")

def main():
    print("Starting Plugin starting...")
    
    try:
        asyncio.run(handle_websocket())
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\n🛑 Shutting down...")
        unregister_ui()
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error: {e}")
        unregister_ui()
    finally:
        print("👋 Plugin stopped")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

---

## Common Pitfalls

### ❌ Registering UI Too Early

**Incorrect:**

```python
def main():
    register_ui()  # TOO EARLY!
    asyncio.run(handle_websocket())
```

**Correct:**

```python
async def handle_websocket():
    async with websockets.connect(WS_URL) as ws:
        async for message in ws:
            event = json.loads(message)
            if event.get('type') == 'plugin_initialized':
                register_ui()  # Register AFTER initialization
```

**Why:** Lunacy's plugin system isn't ready yet. Always wait for `plugin_initialized`.

---

### ❌ Wrong Event Field Names

**Incorrect:**

```json
{ "event": "show_ui", "pluginId": "..." }
```

**Correct:**

```json
{ "type": "show_ui", "pluginId": "..." }
```

All events use `"type"` field, not `"event"`.

---

### ❌ Wrong HTTP Method for getpluginuivalues

**Incorrect:**

```python
response = requests.get(f"{API}/getpluginuivalues?pluginId={PLUGIN_ID}")
```

**Correct:**

```python
response = requests.post(f"{API}/getpluginuivalues", json=PLUGIN_ID)
```

Use POST with pluginId in body, not GET with query string.

---

### ❌ Not Parsing Values

**Incorrect:**

```javascript
const quality = values.quality;  // String "80"
if (quality > 50) { ... }  // String comparison!
```

**Correct:**

```javascript
const quality = parseFloat(values.quality);  // Number 80
if (quality > 50) { ... }  // Numeric comparison
```

All field values are strings - always parse numbers/booleans.

---

### ❌ Not Unregistering UI

**Incorrect:**

```javascript
await processValues();
process.exit(0);  // Dialog stays open!
```

**Correct:**

```javascript
try {
  await processValues();
} finally {
  await axios.post(`${API}/unregisterui`, PLUGIN_ID);
}
```

Always cleanup UI before exiting.

---

### ❌ Not Checking eventType

**Incorrect:**

```javascript
if (fieldId === 'apply') {
  doSomething();
}
```

**Correct:**

```javascript
if (fieldId === 'apply' && eventType === 'click') {
  doSomething();
}
```

Always verify both `fieldId` and `eventType`.

---

### ❌ PluginId Mismatch

**Incorrect:**

```javascript
await axios.post(`${API}/registerui`, { pluginId: 'my-plugin', ... });
const values = await axios.post(`${API}/getpluginuivalues`, "myPlugin");  // Mismatch!
```

**Correct:**

```javascript
const PLUGIN_ID = 'my-plugin';
await axios.post(`${API}/registerui`, { pluginId: PLUGIN_ID, ... });
const values = await axios.post(`${API}/getpluginuivalues`, PLUGIN_ID);
```

Use constant to avoid typos.

---

## External UI

Plugin can launch external UI as separate application.

### Web UI (Express + Browser)

```javascript
const express = require('express');
const axios = require('axios');
const open = require('open');

const app = express();
const LUNACY_API = 'http://localhost:31415';

app.use(express.json());
app.use(express.static('public'));

app.get('/api/selection', async (req, res) => {
  const response = await axios.get(`${LUNACY_API}/getselected`);
  res.json(response.data);
});

app.post('/api/update', async (req, res) => {
  await axios.post(`${LUNACY_API}/updatelayers`, req.body.layers);
  res.json({ success: true });
});

app.listen(3000, async () => {
  console.log('Web UI running on http://localhost:3000');
  await open('http://localhost:3000');
});
```

### Desktop UI (Electron)

```javascript
const { app, BrowserWindow, ipcMain } = require('electron');
const axios = require('axios');

const LUNACY_API = 'http://localhost:31415';

app.on('ready', () => {
  const win = new BrowserWindow({
    width: 800,
    height: 600,
    webPreferences: {
      nodeIntegration: true,
      contextIsolation: false
    }
  });
  
  win.loadFile('index.html');
});

ipcMain.handle('lunacy:get-selection', async () => {
  const response = await axios.get(`${LUNACY_API}/getselected`);
  return response.data;
});

ipcMain.handle('lunacy:update', async (event, layers) => {
  await axios.post(`${LUNACY_API}/updatelayers`, layers);
});
```

### Real-Time Updates (WebSocket Proxy)

Proxy Lunacy events to web clients:

```javascript
const WebSocket = require('ws');

const lunacyWs = new WebSocket('ws://localhost:31416');
const webClients = new Set();

lunacyWs.on('message', (data) => {
  const event = JSON.parse(data);
  
  // Forward to all web clients
  webClients.forEach(client => {
    if (client.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) {
      client.send(JSON.stringify(event));
    }
  });
});

const wsServer = new WebSocket.Server({ port: 3001 });
wsServer.on('connection', (ws) => {
  webClients.add(ws);
  ws.on('close', () => webClients.delete(ws));
});
```

---

## Best Practices

### Parse Values Correctly

All field values are strings:

```javascript
const quality = parseFloat(values.quality);
const includeHidden = values.includeHidden === 'true';
const count = parseInt(values.count);
```

### Always Unregister UI

```javascript
try {
  await performWork();
} finally {
  await axios.post(`${API}/unregisterui`, PLUGIN_ID);
}
```

### Use Descriptive Labels

```javascript
// Good
{ label: "Export Quality (0-100%)" }
{ label: "Include Hidden Layers" }

// Bad
{ label: "Quality" }
{ label: "Hidden" }
```

### Group Related Fields

```javascript
fields: [
  { id: 'format', type: 'select', label: 'Format', options: ['PNG', 'JPEG'] },
  { id: 'quality', type: 'slider', label: 'Quality', min: 0, max: 100 },
  
  { type: 'separator', label: 'Output Options' },
  
  { id: 'filename', type: 'text', label: 'File Name' },
  { id: 'path', type: 'text', label: 'Output Path' }
]
```

### Set Sensible Defaults

```javascript
{ id: 'quality', type: 'slider', value: '80', min: 0, max: 100 }
{ id: 'scale', type: 'number', value: '2', min: 0.5, max: 4 }
```

### Use Tooltips

Add descriptions to help users:

```javascript
{
  id: 'quality',
  type: 'slider',
  label: 'Quality',
  value: '80',
  description: 'Export quality (0-100%). Higher values produce larger files.'
}
```

### Handle Presets Properly

When implementing preset system:

1. **Apply preset** - Update all fields via `/updateuifields`
2. **Detect manual changes** - Reset preset to "Custom" when user modifies field
3. **Listen to value_change events** - Track when user overrides preset

---
