# Plugin automation workflows
Source: https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/raw/plugin-workflows.md

Complete examples for discovery, revision checks, validation, mutations and recovery

This complete reference is synchronized from the [lunacy-plugins article](https://github.com/icons8/lunacy-plugins/blob/7b82b78118e2c66a474f3d556b171903af12bcbc/docs/AUTOMATION_WORKFLOWS.md) at commit `7b82b781`, checked on November 5, 2026. See [Plugins](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugins/) for installation and manifests.

These examples use the preview [Automation API v2](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-v2/). They need a matching Lunacy build; probe `/v2/get_session` instead of assuming an installed release includes them. HTTP requests contain the documented body directly. The grouped MCP/AI Chat `request.operation` wrapper is not part of HTTP.

The sequence is discovery → explicit target → revision → validation → commit → readback. Run examples on a document you intend to edit. Placeholders in JSON, such as `<document-handle>`, must be replaced with actual discovered values.

## A complete variable workflow

Save this as `brand.mjs` and run it with Node.js 18 or newer. It deliberately captures the active document once, verifies that it is ready/editable, and retains that handle. It never chooses the first editable tab after another tab becomes active. The example creates a collection and color variable; it stops if a matching collection already exists so repeated execution does not duplicate resources.

```javascript
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';

const baseUrl = process.env.LUNACY_API ?? 'http://localhost:31415';

async function api(operation, body = {}) {
  const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/v2/${operation}`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify(body)
  });
  const text = await response.text();
  let envelope;
  try {
    envelope = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    throw new Error(`Expected a v2 response for ${operation}; HTTP ${response.status}`);
  }
  if (!response.ok || envelope.ok !== true) {
    const error = new Error(envelope.error?.message ?? `HTTP ${response.status}`);
    error.code = envelope.error?.code;
    error.path = envelope.error?.path;
    error.operationIndex = envelope.error?.operationIndex;
    error.envelope = envelope;
    throw error;
  }
  for (const warning of envelope.warnings ?? []) {
    console.warn(warning);
  }
  return envelope;
}

const session = (await api('get_session')).data;
if (!session.operations.some(item => item.tool === 'apply_variable_changes')) {
  throw new Error('This build does not advertise variable automation');
}
const documents = (await api('list_documents')).data.items;
const chosen = documents.find(item => item.documentHandle === session.activeDocumentHandle);
if (!chosen || chosen.state !== 'ready' || !chosen.canEdit) {
  throw new Error('Choose an editable ready document in Lunacy before running this example');
}
const documentHandle = chosen.documentHandle;

async function currentRevision() {
  const items = (await api('list_documents')).data.items;
  const document = items.find(item => item.documentHandle === documentHandle);
  if (!document?.canEdit || document.state !== 'ready') {
    throw new Error('The chosen document is no longer editable/ready');
  }
  return document.revision;
}

let cursor;
do {
  const result = await api('query_design_system', {
    documentHandle, kinds: ['collection'], scopes: ['local'], query: 'Plugin demo',
    ...(cursor ? { cursor } : {})
  });
  if (result.data.items.some(item => item.name === 'Plugin demo')) {
    throw new Error('Plugin demo already exists: inspect/reuse it instead of creating another collection');
  }
  cursor = result.data.nextCursor;
} while (cursor);

const changes = [
  {
    action: 'createCollection', clientId: 'brand', name: 'Plugin demo',
    defaultThemeName: 'Light', defaultThemeClientId: 'light'
  },
  {
    action: 'createVariable', clientId: 'primary', collection: { clientRef: 'brand' },
    name: 'Primary', type: 'color',
    values: [{ theme: { clientRef: 'light' }, value: { kind: 'literal', value: '0A84FF' } }]
  }
];

await api('apply_variable_changes', {
  documentHandle, expectedRevision: await currentRevision(),
  requestId: randomUUID(), validateOnly: true, changes
});

// A preview does not reserve IDs or a revision. The commit is a new operation.
const committed = await api('apply_variable_changes', {
  documentHandle, expectedRevision: await currentRevision(),
  requestId: randomUUID(), changes
});
const ids = committed.data.clientIds;
const readback = await api('get_design_system_assets', {
  documentHandle,
  assets: [{ kind: 'variable', scope: 'local', id: ids.primary, collectionId: ids.brand }]
});
for (const item of readback.data.items) {
  if (item.error) {
    throw new Error(`${item.error.code}: ${item.error.message}`);
  }
  console.log(JSON.stringify(item.definition, null, 2));
}
```

The variable batch produces one undo item. Request IDs must remain available to the plugin until the result is known. If this example loses its commit response, use the recovery procedure below before running it again. A production plugin should store the exact request before sending it. Do not add automatic mutation retries with a new ID.

For an alias, use the same variable type and a typed selector:

```json
{
  "kind": "alias",
  "variable": {"id": "<same-type-variable-id>"}
}
```

Create a new theme by copying an existing one. `selectCollectionTheme` changes the inspector preview; `setLayerTheme` changes the evaluated canvas theme:

```json
{
  "documentHandle": "<document-handle>",
  "expectedRevision": "<current-revision>",
  "requestId": "<new-request-id>",
  "changes": [
    {
      "action": "createTheme", "clientId": "dark", "name": "Dark",
      "collection": {"id": "<collection-id>"}, "sourceTheme": {"id": "<light-theme-id>"}
    },
    {
      "action": "setLayerTheme", "layerIds": ["<frame-layer-id>"],
      "collection": {"id": "<collection-id>"}, "theme": {"clientRef": "dark"}
    }
  ]
}
```

Send that body to `/v2/apply_variable_changes`. Themes are collection-specific. For a binding, use `get_session.data.bindings` to check the actual property/type/target combination, then send an explicit layer/style reference. For example, binding a float variable to an eligible layer's opacity:

```json
{
  "documentHandle": "<document-handle>",
  "expectedRevision": "<current-revision>",
  "requestId": "<new-request-id>",
  "changes": [{
    "action": "bind", "variable": {"id": "<float-variable-id>"},
    "target": {"kind": "layer", "resource": {"id": "<layer-id>"}},
    "location": {"property": "opacity"}
  }]
}
```

Read `/v2/get_design_context` with `layerIds` afterwards to inspect the binding, resolved theme and effective value. `unbind` uses the same target/location without `variable` and materializes the current effective or cached value.

## Create and apply a shared style

Search first with `query_design_system` using `kinds:["style"]`, `styleType:"color"`, and the intended scopes. Inspect any match with `get_design_system_assets`. If a new style is needed, `/v2/apply_style_changes` can create and apply it in one batch:

```json
{
  "documentHandle": "<document-handle>",
  "expectedRevision": "<current-revision>",
  "requestId": "<new-request-id>",
  "changes": [
    {"action": "create", "clientId": "accent", "name": "Accent", "type": "color", "value": {"fill": "0A84FF"}},
    {"action": "apply", "style": {"clientRef": "accent"}, "targets": [{"layerId": "<layer-id>", "slot": "fills"}]}
  ]
}
```

For text/effect/guide styles, provide the matching `text`/`effects`/`guides` slot. `createFromLayer` captures native appearance rather than requiring a handwritten FREE fragment. A `range` uses UTF-16 `start`/`length` and is supported only on eligible text slots. Inspect `get_asset_usage` before deletion; the default `rejectIfUsed` prevents an accidental destructive detach. `detachConsumers` is an explicit deletion policy.

## Create a component and place an instance

Query component assets first. The summary's `componentId` identifies a definition; `layerId` identifies its source layer. They are different. When an existing reusable component meets the need, pass its returned component reference directly to `createInstances`.

For a new definition from an existing eligible layer, send this to `/v2/apply_component_changes`:

```json
{
  "documentHandle": "<document-handle>",
  "expectedRevision": "<current-revision>",
  "requestId": "<new-request-id>",
  "changes": [
    {
      "action": "createFromLayers", "clientId": "button", "name": "Button",
      "layerIds": ["<frame-layer-id>"], "placement": {"pageId": "<page-id>"}
    },
    {
      "action": "createInstances", "component": {"clientRef": "button"},
      "instances": [{"clientId": "first", "placement": {"pageId": "<page-id>", "x": 40, "y": 40}}]
    }
  ]
}
```

`clientRef` resolves only a preceding compatible creation in this batch. After committing, discover the created asset again when you need its source-layer identity, definition/state owner, or complete typed asset reference. Do not assume every returned `clientIds` entry represents the same resource kind.

A property definition is a typed union. For example, append an explicit property action to a suitable component batch:

```json
{
  "action": "createProperty", "clientId": "caption",
  "component": {"id": "<component-id>"},
  "property": {"type": "text", "name": "Caption", "initialValue": "Continue"}
}
```

Assign values to local instances with `setInstanceProperties`, using the returned property identity:

```json
{
  "action": "setInstanceProperties",
  "instances": [{"id": "<instance-layer-id>"}],
  "properties": [{"property": {"id": "<property-id>"}, "value": {"kind": "text", "value": "Save"}}]
}
```

Creating the property does not invent bindings on source nodes. If a source text/visibility/swap binding is needed, use the documented native `updateDefinition.patch.binds` shape with actual property IDs after creation/readback. A raw FREE fragment cannot resolve a batch `clientRef` string. Imported source definitions remain read-only. See [component semantics](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-v2/#components-and-instances) for states, swaps, supported patch fields and override categories.

## Pages, navigation and document lifecycle

`list_documents` discovers visible tabs; `activate_document` takes `tabId` and a request ID. Loading and navigation are explicit operations rather than consequences of a read. To create a local document:

```json
{"name": "Plugin draft", "requestId": "<new-request-id>"}
```

Send that to `/v2/create_document`, then retain its returned document handle, revision and initial page. For an existing file, `/v2/open_document` accepts exactly one of these locator shapes:

```json
{"localPath": "<user-authorized-absolute-file-path>", "requestId": "<new-request-id>"}
```

```json
{"cloud": {"documentId": "<document-id>", "versionId": "<optional-version-id>"}, "requestId": "<new-request-id>"}
```

Omit `versionId` to open the current cloud document. The application needs its normal account/file access; the API does not grant it. Version tabs can be read-only. `open_document` reuses a matching visible tab where supported.

Create and rename a page in a single `/v2/manage_pages` batch:

```json
{
  "documentHandle": "<document-handle>",
  "expectedRevision": "<current-revision>",
  "requestId": "<new-request-id>",
  "changes": [
    {"action": "create", "clientId": "screens", "name": "Screens"},
    {"action": "rename", "page": {"clientRef": "screens"}, "name": "Product screens"}
  ]
}
```

Activate the returned page with `/v2/activate_page`, supplying `pageId` plus the document mutation guards. Navigation does not advance content revision or add an undo item. Page edits do. Deleting a nonempty page requires the explicit `deleteContents` policy; default `rejectIfNotEmpty` rejects it, and the final page cannot be removed.

Rename with `/v2/rename_document` and `name` plus guards. Save to an authorized destination through `/v2/save_document`:

```json
{
  "documentHandle": "<document-handle>", "expectedRevision": "<current-revision>",
  "requestId": "<new-request-id>", "destination": "<user-authorized-absolute-free-path>",
  "overwrite": false, "allowDialog": false
}
```

Inspect `savedRevision`, `destination`, and the returned document's `save` metadata. A cloud queued/sent result is not an extra durable-storage guarantee. Do not close after a failed/cancelled save. When the intended document is safely saved, close with `/v2/close_document`:

```json
{
  "tabId": "<tab-id>", "documentHandle": "<document-handle>",
  "expectedRevision": "<current-revision>", "requestId": "<new-request-id>", "ifUnsaved": "fail"
}
```

Every loaded close needs both handle and revision. `ifUnsaved:"discard"` is destructive and must reflect an explicit user decision. Unloaded/failed tabs use the metadata-only close path. `reorder_tabs` supplies the exact complete visible tab ID set in its desired order.

## Recover a response without duplicating a change

Keep the exact original request and its scope. If the transport failed after sending a document mutation, call `/v2/get_request_status`:

```json
{"documentHandle": "<original-document-handle>", "requestId": "<original-request-id>"}
```

Use `tabId` for a tab-scoped lifecycle request, or neither selector for a session-scoped operation. Do not change scope because the active tab changed.

- `pending`: the original request is still in progress; wait rather than start a different mutation.
- `completed`: inspect `data.result`, which is the original success/error envelope, including returned IDs.
- `unknown`: retention expired, the server restarted, or the request was never observed. Reread model/save/tab state before deciding what to do next.

An exact retry with the same payload/target/request ID can return the retained result even if its old `expectedRevision` is now stale. A different payload with the same ID returns `RequestConflict`. A new request ID means a new operation; it is not a safe lost-response retry. A known `RevisionConflict` requires a fresh read and rebuilt request; never just replace the revision on a destructive stale plan.

## Discover and import library assets

These are request examples, not an instruction to connect/publish anything. Use already authorized account sources. `/v2/list_libraries` with `scope:"available"` lists metadata; follow `nextCursor` with the same target/filter. A metadata `version:null` is not a usable import version.

Search one explicitly selected source through `/v2/query_design_system`:

```json
{
  "documentHandle": "<target-document-handle>", "libraryIds": ["<discovered-library-id>"],
  "scopes": ["availableLibrary"], "kinds": ["component"], "query": "Button", "limit": 50
}
```

Retain the returned asset reference and `sourceVersion` together. Inspect the definition before importing. Then send `/v2/import_library_assets` with the current target revision:

```json
{
  "documentHandle": "<target-document-handle>", "expectedRevision": "<current-target-revision>",
  "requestId": "<new-request-id>", "libraryId": "<discovered-library-id>",
  "sourceVersion": "<observed-semantic-source-version>", "validateOnly": true,
  "assets": [{"kind": "component", "id": "<source-component-id>", "scope": "availableLibrary", "libraryId": "<discovered-library-id>"}]
}
```

Commit with `validateOnly:false`, a fresh request ID and current target revision after a successful preview. Use the returned `assets[].local` mapping for local consumers. Existing imported IDs are reused; importing a new asset does not implicitly update existing imported dependencies.

Persistent `connect_library`/`disconnect_library` needs an editable cloud target and a discovered cloud locator. A local target has no persistent connections but can discover/import available sources. Disconnecting retains imported assets and their consumers. Source definitions are not made editable by importing them.

To refresh, first inspect the source again and submit explicit version pairs to `/v2/refresh_libraries`:

```json
{
  "documentHandle": "<target-document-handle>", "expectedRevision": "<current-target-revision>",
  "requestId": "<new-request-id>",
  "libraries": [{"libraryId": "<discovered-library-id>", "version": "<observed-semantic-source-version>"}]
}
```

Read every result item: refresh is atomic per library, and successful earlier libraries remain applied if a later one fails. Missing source assets are not automatically deleted. Review [native library limits](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-v2/#libraries) before preparing large imports.

## Combine v2 with legacy layer, export and UI calls

Use v2 for explicit document discovery and typed design-system operations. Legacy layer/image/export routes keep their own bodies and response formats. On a matching build, pass request-local target headers rather than switching the active tab:

```javascript
const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/getlayersbyids`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'X-Lunacy-Document-Handle': documentHandle,
    'X-Lunacy-Page-Id': pageId
  },
  body: JSON.stringify(layerIds)
});
const raw = await response.text();
if (!response.ok) {
  throw new Error(`Layer read failed: HTTP ${response.status}`);
}
const layers = JSON.parse(raw);
```

`pageId` and `layerIds` in this fragment must come from the chosen document. Only pass a page header on routes supporting it. Target failures are explicit; do not retry against the active tab. Legacy calls do not gain a v2 envelope/replay guard from these headers. See the [legacy endpoint reference](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api/#explicit-document-targets).

The [UI guide](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-ui/) and [service example](https://github.com/icons8/lunacy-plugins/tree/7b82b78118e2c66a474f3d556b171903af12bcbc/featured-plugins/bitmap-to-vector-plugin) show registration and WebSocket lifecycle. Re-register UI after each `plugin_initialized` handshake. Events signal that you should reread; legacy document IDs are not live v2 handles and an event is not a complete revision/commit acknowledgement.


# Plugins
Source: https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/raw/plugins.md

Install plugins and build integrations with the Lunacy Automation API

## What a Lunacy plugin is

A plugin is an external program that uses Lunacy's local Automation API. It can inspect a document, create or edit layers, work with components and variables, export assets, subscribe to application events, and provide a plugin UI. Plugins can be written in any language that can make HTTP requests; the public repository includes Node.js, Python, and C# examples.

The application supplies the editing operations and their undo behavior. A plugin does not load a managed assembly into the editor or need to implement Lunacy's document model.

### Availability

This guide covers the existing plugin interface and the new typed v2 API and grouped automation catalog, checked on November 5, 2026. The v2 API and the 11-group MCP/AI Chat catalog require a build that includes them; they are not a guarantee about every released Lunacy build. Ask the running application for `GET /v2/get_session`. A missing route means that build does not expose this v2 interface.

The complete references are available on this site:

- [Plugin API reference](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api/) — legacy geometry, screenshots, export, events, and plugin UI.
- [Plugin UI guide](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-ui/) — complete field definitions and service lifecycle examples.
- [Automation workflows](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-workflows/) — runnable examples and recovery.
- [Typed API v2 reference](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-v2/) — all 26 methods, request/result contracts, actions, limits, and errors.
- [MCP](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/mcp/) — connect an external AI client to the grouped tools.
- [AI Chat](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/ai-chat/) — use the same automation from Lunacy's built-in chat.

For runnable examples and development articles, use [lunacy-plugins](https://github.com/icons8/lunacy-plugins), its [API v2 reference](https://github.com/icons8/lunacy-plugins/blob/7b82b78118e2c66a474f3d556b171903af12bcbc/docs/API_V2_REFERENCE.md), and [automation workflows](https://github.com/icons8/lunacy-plugins/blob/7b82b78118e2c66a474f3d556b171903af12bcbc/docs/AUTOMATION_WORKFLOWS.md).

## Install a plugin

1. Get a plugin from a source you trust and read its runtime/dependency instructions.
2. In Lunacy, use **Help → Open App Data Folder**. Open or create its `Plugins` directory.
3. Put the plugin in its own immediate subdirectory. Its `plugin.jsonc` must be at that directory's root. `plugin.json` is also accepted.
4. Install any runtime/dependencies required by that plugin.
5. Restart Lunacy and use the plugin's command in the Plugins menu.

The actual application-data location depends on the platform and package variant. Use the menu command rather than copying a path from another computer or package.

Plugins run programs with your user's operating-system permissions. Inspect a plugin before installing it. The local connection does not prevent the plugin from sending data to another service.

## Manifest and lifecycle

A minimal utility plugin can contain these two files:

```text
inspect-document/
  plugin.jsonc
  inspect.js
```

`plugin.jsonc`:

```json
{
  "id": "example-inspect-document",
  "name": "Inspect document",
  "lifecycle": "Utility",
  "commands": [
    {
      "id": "inspect",
      "name": "Inspect open documents",
      "executable": "node",
      "args": ["inspect.js"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Use relative script paths. The default working directory is the plugin directory. The executable and arguments are separate values; do not rely on shell-specific quoting for paths with spaces.

| Lifecycle | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `Utility` | Run a command when the user chooses it. Appropriate for one-off inspection, changes, or export. |
| `Service` | Run a longer-lived process through `serviceCommand`, for example an event-driven integration or plugin UI. Subscribe only to the event categories the plugin needs. |

### Manifest fields

| Field | Type / purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Stable plugin identity; use the same value in registration and UI requests. |
| `name` | Display name. |
| `description`, `version` | Optional descriptive strings. |
| `workingDirectory` | Optional process working directory; defaults to the installed plugin directory. |
| `lifecycle` | `"Utility"` (default) or `"Service"`. |
| `commands` | Array of command objects for utility menu actions. |
| `serviceCommand` | Command object used to launch a service plugin. |
| `events` | Optional application event category names: `selection`, `undo`, `document`, `window`. |

A command object has `id`, `name`, `executable`, an `args` string array, and optional `description`, `env` string dictionary, and `timeoutMs` integer. `timeoutMs` controls a utility command's execution timeout; it is not a service lifetime setting. The process inherits its environment and applies the declared `env` overrides. Use a real executable path or a runtime discoverable by the application process; a shell alias is not an executable.

For a service plugin, replace the utility `commands` entry with a `serviceCommand` and set `lifecycle` to `"Service"`. Connect its WebSocket, register the same plugin ID, and wait for `plugin_initialized` before registering a UI. The service is started with the application and participates in application shutdown; do not use a short utility command for a persistent subscription.

The [plugin API reference](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api/) covers events and connection messages. The complete [plugin UI guide](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-ui/) describes registration, field types, values and lifecycle examples. The [repository examples](https://github.com/icons8/lunacy-plugins/tree/main) demonstrate each pattern.

## First request

Use a Node.js runtime with built-in `fetch` for this example. `inspect.js` lists tabs without loading all documents:

```js
const baseUrl = process.argv[2] || 'http://localhost:31415';

async function call(method, body = {}) {
  const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/v2/${method}`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify(body)
  });
  const result = await response.json();
  if (!response.ok || !result.ok) {
    throw new Error(`${result.error?.code || response.status}: ${result.error?.message || 'Request failed'}`);
  }
  return result;
}

async function main() {
  const session = await call('get_session');
  const documents = await call('list_documents');
  console.log('API version:', session.data.apiVersion);
  console.log(documents.data.items);
}

main().catch(error => {
  console.error(error.message);
  process.exitCode = 1;
});
```

The default HTTP address is `http://localhost:31415`. If your application instance uses another endpoint, pass its actual base URL to the plugin. Use the running application's endpoint and operation metadata; do not infer capabilities from a documentation version alone.

## Edit the intended document

A safe workflow is:

1. Read the session and tab list.
2. Choose the intended item using its name and persisted identity. Activate an unloaded tab only when loading is needed.
3. Keep the returned live `documentHandle` and `revision`. They identify this instance and state, not every document with the same name.
4. Search existing assets and read their definitions/usages before creating duplicates.
5. Send a typed batch with `expectedRevision` and a unique `requestId`. Use `validateOnly:true` before a complex or destructive change.
6. Read back the affected data and use the returned revision for the next edit.
7. Save only when the workflow calls for saving. A failed save must not be reported as complete.

For example, create a variable collection through the HTTP API:

```json
{
  "documentHandle": "<live-handle>",
  "expectedRevision": "<current-revision>",
  "requestId": "<unique-request-id>",
  "validateOnly": true,
  "changes": [
    {"action":"createCollection","clientId":"brand","name":"Brand","defaultThemeName":"Light"}
  ]
}
```

POST that body to `/v2/apply_variable_changes`, replacing placeholders with real values. Validation creates no live collection or history. To commit, use `validateOnly:false`, a fresh request ID, and a current revision. One committed domain batch creates one undo operation; an equal-value no-op creates none.

A creation may declare `clientId`. A later compatible change in the same ordered batch can reference it with `{"clientRef":"brand"}`. An existing asset uses `{"id":"<asset-id>"}`. Do not send both selectors, reuse a forward/deleted reference, or treat a validation preview ID as a persisted ID.

## Errors and uncertain responses

For v2, inspect both the HTTP status and the JSON envelope. Success has `ok:true`; failure has `ok:false` and a stable `error.code`. Legacy routes retain their older text/JSON/binary responses.

If a response is lost, retry the same target, request ID, and payload, or use `/v2/get_request_status`. A different payload with the same retained request ID fails with `RequestConflict`. Once status is `unknown`, reread the document before choosing a new request ID: a fresh ID could repeat a creation, save, import, or discard.

On `RevisionConflict`, reread and rebuild the edit. On `Busy`, wait for the relevant operation/layout to finish. On permission or filesystem denial, obtain access through the normal application workflow; an HTTP client cannot grant itself access.

## Components, libraries, and persistence

Use the domain methods for assets rather than rebuilding them through layer JSON. Component properties, states, overrides, style links, variable themes, and aliases have native identity and inheritance rules.

Imported library definitions are read-only. Editing a source requires opening the source document with edit access and using that source's own live handle. Connecting or importing is not permission to publish. Persistent connect/disconnect operations apply to editable cloud documents; local documents can inspect and import explicitly available assets. Disconnecting does not delete imported consumers.

Local save completion reports the actual destination and saved revision. Cloud results distinguish queued/pending/sent synchronization from durable server storage. Read the result instead of inferring success from a request completing or the document looking clean.

FREE geometry and the saved `.free` archive are documented in the [FREE format reference](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/free-format/). HTTP envelopes, live handles, replay entries, and chat history are separate contracts.

## Next steps

Use the [complete typed API](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api-v2/) for all actions and exact fields, or the [legacy/events/UI reference](https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/plugin-api/) to extend an existing plugin. The [repository workflow article](https://github.com/icons8/lunacy-plugins/blob/7b82b78118e2c66a474f3d556b171903af12bcbc/docs/AUTOMATION_WORKFLOWS.md) provides request sequences and recovery examples.


# Private Cloud
Source: https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/raw/private_cloud.md

How to collaborate in total privacy

Many industries feel uneasy knowing that their data is floating somewhere in the clouds without proper control — banking, healthcare, insurance, you name it.

For design teams working in such fields, Lunacy offers a **Private Cloud** solution with two deployment options: **on-premises** and **virtual private server (VPS)**.

## Private cloud on-premises

For companies with a strong focus on security who prefer to keep all their data in-house. 

**How it works**

- You deploy your personal Lunacy Cloud on a dedicated server within your corporate network.
- You configure the teams and control who can edit or view certain documents.
- You take full care of the server and backups.
- Your administrator installs the updates after all the required checks.

**What you get**

- Total control over your design cloud.
- Happy design and other teams enjoying the perks that cloud collaboration brings.
- Happy security department since no data gets outside.


## Private cloud on VPS

This option is for the teams that don’t feel like sharing a common cloud with the rest of the world but aren’t quite ready to manage their own servers. 

**How it works**

- Our engineers deploy, configure, and update Lunacy Private Cloud for you on a virtual private server in any region or jurisdiction.
- You configure the teams and control who can edit or view certain documents.
- You make backups of your documents or delegate it to our engineers.
- Our engineers assist you with any technical matters as needed.
- Unlike users of privately hosted clouds, you can keep using built-in graphics and Lunacy’s AI tools.

**What you get**

- Efficient design team working in a modern collaborative design editor.
- Peace of mind about the security of your design data.
- No headache about managing your private design cloud.


Both solutions, Private Cloud on-premises and VPS, come with *24/7 priority support*, a *dedicated customer success manager*, and *priority feature requests*.

Contact us, to [request a demo](https://ic8.link/B9oI8).

# Prototyping
Source: https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/raw/prototyping.md

Learn how to create interactive prototypes in Lunacy

Prototypes make your design interactive, letting you communicate both aesthetics and user experience.

## Creating a prototype

<div class="callout callout--info">
    <p><strong>Note:</strong> If you are planning to add prototyping to your project, the use of frames is a must.</p>
</div>

To create a prototype, you typically need three key elements:  

- **Hotspot** – an interactive zone that triggers an action. It can be an entire frame or a specific element within a frame, like a button or menu option. You can turn any selected frame or element into a hotspot by pressing `H` or clicking `+` in the Prototyping section of the right panel.  

  You can also create dedicated hotspot layers, which are useful when an element is too small to interact with comfortably. By adding a hotspot layer over it, you can enlarge the clickable area. To do this, select the **Hotspot tool** from the toolbar (or press `H` when nothing is selected) and draw the hotspot layer wherever needed.  

- **Connection** – a visual arrow that links the hotspot to its destination, defining the flow of the interaction.  

- **Destination** – the target frame or a specific location within a frame where the interaction will take the user.  


The video below shows an example of creating a simple prototype.

<video autoplay="" muted="" loop="" playsinline="" width="auto" poster="/public/prototyping_linking_frames.png" height="auto"><source src="/public/simpleprototypev11.mp4" type="video/mp4"></video>

What happens in the video:  

1. We select **Frame 1**, click `+` in the **Prototyping** section, and link it to **Frame 2**. This makes the entire frame interactive—clicking anywhere on it (default action) navigates to Frame 2.  
2. In **Frame 2**, we create a **hotspot** over the icon and text block, grouping them into a single interactive zone. We then link this hotspot back to **Frame 1**.  
3. Pressing `F5` opens the **prototype player**. Clicking anywhere in Frame 1 takes us to Frame 2. If we click outside the interactive zone in Frame 2, the player highlights the clickable area.  
4. Pressing `Esc` exits the prototype player.  

The **Prototyping** section offers various settings to help you design more complex prototypes with diverse animations, transitions, and interaction flows.

## Prototyping settings

When setting up an interaction in your prototype, think of it as answering a few key questions:

* **On what event?** (Trigger)
* **What happens?** (Action)
* **If it moves, where to?** (Destination)
* **What does it look like?** (Animation)
* **What happens if it is scrolled?** (Behavior on scroll)


The figure below explains the prototyping settings. Experimenting with these options will bring your designs to life with natural interactions.

<embed type="image/svg+xml" alt="prototyping_settingsv11" src="https://cdn-eu.icons8.com/docs/Dko8QE6mZ06fz2gAGGUBbA/y4w8lTEO4UeyEQCWaUYfmA.svg" /> 


### Triggers

Triggers define what starts an interaction in your prototype.

| **Trigger**        | **What it does**                                    | **Example use case**                         |
|--------------------|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| **On click**      | Activates when the user clicks on an element.     | Toggle a dropdown menu when clicking a button. |
| **On drag**       | Triggers when an element is dragged.              | Swipe between frames.             |
| **While hovering** | Runs as long as the cursor stays over an element. | Change the color of a button when hovered. (You'll need to have a component with different states to switch between them)|
| **While pressing**| Active while the user holds down a click or key.  | Show an animation while pressing a button. |
| **Key**           | Responds to a specific keyboard input.            | Press "Esc" to close a popup window.       |
| **Mouse enter**   | Fires when the cursor moves over an element.      | Expand a sidebar when the cursor enters its area. |
| **Mouse leave**   | Fires when the cursor moves away from an element. | Collapse a sidebar when the cursor leaves it. |
| **Mouse up**      | Triggers when a pressed mouse button is released. | Releasing the mouse dismisses a pop-up window. |
| **Mouse down**    | Triggers when a mouse button is pressed.          | Pressing a card makes it pop out slightly. |
| **After delay**   | Runs automatically after a set time.              | Show a notification after a few seconds.   |

### Actions
The action determines what happens next in the prototype after a trigger.

| **Action type**    | **What it does**                              | **Example use case**                                  |
|-------------------|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| **Navigate to**   | Moves the user to another frame.          | Clicking a button takes the user to a different screen. |
| **Scroll to**     | Scrolls to a specific section within the same frame. | Clicking "Back to top" smoothly scrolls to the top of the page. |
| **Open URL**      | Opens an external link in a browser.       | Clicking a "Learn more" button takes the user to a website. |
| **Back**         | Returns to the previous screen. This action type requires no links.        | A "Back" button navigates to the last visited frame. |
| **Open overlay**  | Displays a floating layer over the current screen. | Tapping "Delete" opens a warning. |
| **Swap overlay**  | Replaces the current overlay with another one. | Switching between different steps of a multi-step form. |
| **Close overlay** | Hides the currently active overlay.       | Clicking "X" closes  a pop-up window. |


### Destinations

The destinations dropdown (<embed type="image/svg+xml" alt="Icon 24" src="https://cdn-eu.icons8.com/docs/Dko8QE6mZ06fz2gAGGUBbA/eADidnPOo0GeElwzqXhkFg.svg" />) lists all available frames in the document, including those on other pages. Keeping frame names clear and organized is a good practice, especially in large projects—it will save you time when selecting the right frame.

<div class="callout callout--info">
    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> Hovering over a frame in the list will automatically zoom to it.</p>
</div>

### Animations

Animations define how transitions between frames happen, adding fluidity to interactions. Below is a breakdown of the available animation types and their configuration options.

| **Animation type**  | **What it does**                                       | **Example use case**                                    | **Adjustable settings** |
|--------------------|------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| **Instant**       | Changes the frame immediately, with no transition. | Best for quick jumps between screens without visual effects. | None |
| **Dissolve**      | Fades the current frame into the next one.         | Smooth transitions for modals, pop-ups, or scene changes. | - Effects  <br> - Duration |
| **Move In / Out** | Moves the new frame in or the old frame out from a specified direction. | Creating a slide-in menu or overlay effect. | - Effects  <br> - Direction  <br> - Duration |
| **Push**         | Shifts the current frame out while bringing in the new one from the same direction. | Mimicking page transitions in mobile apps. | - Effects  <br> - Direction  <br> - Duration |
| **Slide In / Out** | Slides a frame into or out of view without affecting other elements. | Great for sidebars, notifications, or contextual menus. | - Effects  <br> - Direction  <br> - Duration |

You can preview how an animation will look and feel by hovering over the preview pane in the prototyping settings.


#### Animation effects

You can choose between the following animation effects:  
- **Linear** – moves at a steady pace without acceleration.  
- **Ease In** – starts slow and gradually speeds up.  
- **Ease Out** – moves quickly at first, then slows down before stopping.  
- **Ease In and Out** – combines both effects: begins slowly, accelerates in the middle, and slows down again.
- **Gentle** – creates a smooth, gradual transition for a soft feel.  
- **Quick** – moves rapidly for a snappy, responsive effect.  
- **Slow** – prolongs the transition for a more relaxed motion.  
- **Bouncy** – adds a playful, spring-like motion to the animation.   
- **Custom** – opens the Bézier curve editor, allowing you to fine-tune the acceleration and deceleration of an animation.

### **Behavior on scroll**  

These options determine how an element behaves when users scroll the prototype:  

- **Scroll** – the element moves along with the rest of the content as users scroll.  
- **Fixed** – the element stays in place while the background scrolls (e.g., floating buttons, support chat bubbles).  
- **Sticky** – the element scrolls normally but becomes fixed once it reaches the top of the prototype.  
- **Keep Scroll Position** – selecting this checkbox, ensures the prototype maintains the current [scroll position](#scrollable-prototypes) when navigating between screens, preventing it from resetting to the top.  

### Scrollable prototypes

<div class="callout callout--info">
    <p><strong>Note:</strong> Scrollable prototypes work only with frames based on <a href="https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/layers/#adding-frames" target="_blank">frame presets</a> (Full HD, iMac, iPhone, etc.).</p>
    <p>If the list of preset frames does not include a frame of the required size, you can <a href="https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/layers/#custom-presets" target="_blank">create a custom preset</a>.</p>
</div>

To **create a scrollable prototype**:

1. Create a frame using a preset.
2. Resize the frame vertically. Resized frames have the label **Resized** in the right panel:

    <embed type="image/svg+xml" alt="Rezsized frame" src="https://cdn-eu.icons8.com/docs/Dko8QE6mZ06fz2gAGGUBbA/GOdSpBpfskmcQGujzSMcPA.svg" /> 

3. Fill the frame with content and link it with other frames.

Preview the prototype as usual and scroll down to test out the interface.

## Previewing prototypes

To **preview a prototype**, select the frame you want to start with and click the **Play** button (<embed type="image/svg+xml" alt="Play" src="https://cdn-eu.icons8.com/docs/Dko8QE6mZ06fz2gAGGUBbA/HD-TYiNcVEy5Npo_ePOa8w.svg" width="20" />) at the top right corner of the interface.

If you want to always preview your prototype from a certain frame:

1. Left-click over the frame.
2. On the context menu, select **Set as Start Point**.
3. Before running the prototype player, make sure that nothing is selected.

<div class="callout callout--info">
    <p><strong>Note:</strong> Selected frames override start points.</p>
</div>

To exit the prototype player, click <embed type="image/svg+xml" alt="Play" src="https://cdn-eu.icons8.com/docs/Dko8QE6mZ06fz2gAGGUBbA/HD-TYiNcVEy5Npo_ePOa8w.svg" width="20" /> again, or press `Esc`.


## Sharing prototype previews

<div class="callout callout--info">
    <p><strong>Note:</strong> This feature is available only in cloud documents. To turn a local document into cloud, click <embed type="image/svg+xml" alt="Upload to cloud" src="https://cdn-eu.icons8.com/docs/Dko8QE6mZ06fz2gAGGUBbA/mhDIDVDjc0yEpQTt-4nylQ.svg" /> 
on the top panel.</p>
</div>

To share a prototype on the web:

1. Click <embed type="image/svg+xml" alt="Play" src="https://cdn-eu.icons8.com/docs/Dko8QE6mZ06fz2gAGGUBbA/HD-TYiNcVEy5Npo_ePOa8w.svg" width="20" /> or press `F5` to start the prototype player.
2. In the top right corner of the player click **Share**, then click **Copy prototype link** to add the link to your clipboard.
3. Send the link to your teammate or reviewer.

<embed type="image/svg+xml" alt="Sharing prototype" src="https://cdn-eu.icons8.com/docs/Dko8QE6mZ06fz2gAGGUBbA/coRUmvl4DU2CZJWjxg8jCA.svg" /> 


People working with the web prototype can leave comments. Before doing this, they will need to log in or sign up.




# Shared libraries
Source: https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/raw/sharedlibraries.md

How to reuse components and styles from other files

In Lunacy, any **cloud file** that contains components and/or layer or text styles can become a library. You can reuse those components and/or styles across other **cloud files**. This will help you speed up your workflow and keep your designs consistent.

To connect a library to a file:

1. In the left panel click **Components** or **Styles**, then click ![library_icon](public/openbook.png).
2. In the displayed window, find the file that you're going to use as a library.
3. In the lower-left corner of the file preview, click **Add**. A list of components/styles from the file will appear in the panel.

<embed type="image/svg+xml" alt="Adding_library" src="https://cdn-eu.icons8.com/docs/Dko8QE6mZ06fz2gAGGUBbA/tMw9ngY2BUC_UZpTbW4m5Q.svg" /> 



Now you can start using the library like any other <a href="https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/components/" target="_blank">components</a> or <a href="https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/layerstyles/" target="_blank">styles</a>.


To disconnect a library from a file:

1. In the left panel, click **Components** or **Styles**, then click ![library_icon](public/openbook.png).
2. In the displayed window, find the library file.
3. In the lower-left corner of the file preview, click **Remove**. The lists of components/styles will disappear.

# Fills, borders, effects
Source: https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/raw/styling.md

Learn how to work with styling options in Lunacy

Use **styling options** to define the color and effects of a layer, including:

- **Fills and tints.** Choose from solid, gradient, or image fills and apply tints to customize the colors.
- **Borders.** Add them to your layers to create clear distinctions or define boundaries.
- **Shadows.** Experiment with outer and inner shadows to add depth and dimension to your elements.
- **Blurs.** Add Gaussian or background blurs to your layers.

These options appear in the right panel whenever you select layer. 

<embed type="image/svg+xml" alt="styling_options" src="https://cdn-eu.icons8.com/docs/Dko8QE6mZ06fz2gAGGUBbA/B5lyWRr6i0CpxecjtRet_w.svg" width="844" /> 

You can apply them to all <a href="https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/layers/#introduction" target="_blank">types of layers</a>, except for <a href="https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/tools/#hotspot-tool" target="_blank">hotspots</a>, and <a href="https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/tools/#slice-tool" target="_blank">slices</a>, though not all layers have all of the styling options available. For example, groups have [tints](#tints) instead of [fills](#fills), and <a href="https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/components/#managing-instances" target="_blank">component instances</a> have both these options.

Save time by <a href="https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/layerstyles/" target="_blank">creating layer styles</a> for individual or multiple styling options. You can easily reuse them across different layers, keeping your designs consistent.

**See also:**<br>
<a href="https://lunacy.docs.icons8.com/layerstyles/" target="_blank">Layer and text styles</a>

## Adding styling options

To **apply a fill, border, or any other styling option** to a layer:

1. Select a layer.
2. Click `+` next to the required styling section in the **right panel**.
3. Adjust the settings to define styling parameters for the layer.

<video autoplay="" muted="" loop="" playsinline="" width="auto" poster="/public/styling_adding_fills_borders_effects.png" height="auto"><source src="/public/styling_adding_fills_borders_effects.mp4" type="video/mp4"></video>

### Managing and deleting styling options

Each layer can have multiple styling options of the same type (except for blurs). For example, you can apply an image fill to a layer and a semi-transparent solid fill on top of it. Also, a layer can have several borders or shadows. Just click the `+` icon to add another styling setting.

To adjust a layer’s appearance, rearrange the order of the styling settings within each section.

<video autoplay="" muted="" loop="" playsinline="" width="auto" poster="/public/styling_moving_fills.png" height="auto"><source src="/public/styling_moving_fills.mp4" type="video/mp4"></video>

You can temporarily hide some of the settings by clicking <embed type="image/svg+xml" alt="eye_hide" src="https://cdn-eu.icons8.com/docs/Dko8QE6mZ06fz2gAGGUBbA/QgphXanfmEC4xSEHsd4zpQ.svg" width="24" />. To delete a styling setting, click <embed type="image/svg+xml" alt="Delete" src="https://cdn-eu.icons8.com/docs/Dko8QE6mZ06fz2gAGGUBbA/atwbWW7Xe0W7xOC5ILLNhQ.svg" width="16" />.

<video autoplay="" muted="" loop="" playsinline="" width="auto" poster="/public/styling_hide_delete.png" height="auto"><source src="/public/styling_hide_delete.mp4" type="video/mp4"></video>

### Applying styling options to multiple layers

To apply styling options to multiple layers, select them and click `+` next to any of the styling sections in the right panel.

<embed type="image/svg+xml" alt="effects_to_multiple_layers" src="https://cdn-eu.icons8.com/docs/Dko8QE6mZ06fz2gAGGUBbA/sPPKm0BlvkOi4bgdTX9PVw.svg" width="844" /> 

If you see **Click + to replace mixed content** in any of the styling sections in the right panel, it means that the selected layers already have different settings for this option. 

Click `+` to override the current settings and apply the same styling option to the selected layers.

<video autoplay="" muted="" loop="" playsinline="" width="auto" poster="/public/styling_to_multiple_layers.png" height="auto"><source src="/public/styling_to_multiple_layers.mp4" type="video/mp4"></video>

## [Fills](#fills)

**Fills** define the color of a layer. Fill options are available in all styling sections (except for blurs) and define the color of the selected layer, borders, or shadows. 

There are several ways to change the fill color. You can:

- Open the color picker/slider by clicking the color swatch in the **Fill** section. 
- Use the **Eyedropper tool** (`I`) and click on a color you want to use for your layer.
- Pick a color variable or a preset color.
- Inside the color picker, type or paste the HEX, RGBA, HSB, or HLS value for a solid fill into the color code input field. 
- Enter the HEX value for solid fills manually into the color text box in the **Fill** section or the color picker.

<div class="callout callout--info">
    <p><strong>Note:</strong> The methods below work for solid fills or parts of a gradient. </p>
</div>

<video autoplay="" muted="" loop="" playsinline="" width="auto" poster="/public/styling_applying_color.png" height="auto"><source src="/public/styling_applying_color.mp4" type="video/mp4"></video>


#### Color picker

To open the **color picker**, click the color swatch in one of the styling sections in the right panel.

<embed type="image/svg+xml" alt="open_color_picker" src="https://cdn-eu.icons8.com/docs/Dko8QE6mZ06fz2gAGGUBbA/nTP37iWiQ0GKG-KXLZgqzg.svg" width="844"  /> 

The color picker displays these settings:

<embed type="image/svg+xml" alt="fill_settings" src="https://cdn-eu.icons8.com/docs/Dko8QE6mZ06fz2gAGGUBbA/1sUgxgbqe0SwBtKhg63UQw.svg" width="844" /> 

**Fill type.** Available for the **Fill** and **Border** color pickers only.

**Color selection box.** This is where you select the color.

**The eyedropper tool.** Click it and use the tool to sample colors from other layers or the interface.

**Color selection slider.** Slide along the bar to switch colors.

**Opacity slider.** Slide along the bar to adjust the opacity.

**Color code.** Displays the code of the currently selected color:<br>
- HEX
- RGB
- HSB
- HSL

**Color code input field.** Paste HEX, RGBA, HSB, or HLS values here for maximum accuracy.

**The opacity entry field.** Manually enter the opacity percentage.

**Create color variable.** This button opens the color variable editing mode.

**Preset colors.** To speed up your work with colors, you can save them here and select them directly from this panel later. There are two types of preset colors:<br>
- **Global** colors appear in the color picker in all documents.<br>
- **Document** colors are available in the current document only.

**Global and document presets.** To switch between global and document colors, open the dropdown menu. To delete a color preset, right-click over it, then select **Remove**.

**Switch view.** Use this button to switch the presets between list and grid views. In list view, you’ll be able to rename colors: right-click a color, then select **Rename**.

**Add color preset.** Use this button to add the currently selected color to **Global** or **Document** presets.

All newly created documents have a color palette which includes document color variables for main, accent, background, and text colors.

To **change palette colors manually**, click on the color swatches to open the color picker.

Using the document color palette, Lunacy applies color to shapes automatically depending on their size and predicted purpose. Larger shapes have background colors while smaller elements are assigned primary or accent colors.

<video autoplay="" muted="" loop="" playsinline="" width="auto" poster="/public/styling_auto_shape.png" height="auto"><source src="/public/styling_auto_shape.mp4" type="video/mp4"></video>

If you want the default shape color to be the usual gray, **delete all palette colors** by pressing <embed type="image/svg+xml" alt="Delete_button" src="https://cdn-eu.icons8.com/docs/Dko8QE6mZ06fz2gAGGUBbA/mzlutszh_UmV3L0QGqvUfg.svg" width="20" > next to each one.
